It's Vann, Chris's husband. I don't often write to you, but I read something that I wanted to share.
The _New York Times_ published a profile of Chris yesterday with the headline: _" His Election Could Decide Senate Control. He Could Make History, Too."_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1b4028a7-73d1-4bbb-9b68-d6b48fc2a4f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/1b4028a7-73d1-4bbb-9b68-d6b48fc2a4f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Both halves of that headline are true. But Chris is only focused on the first one.**
That's who he is. When the _Times_ asked him about making history, he said he isn't thinking much about it, that he's focused every day on the people of New Hampshire. On the trail it's the same: affordable health care, high prices, corruption in Washington. He means every word. It's one of the many reasons I love him.
But I'm his husband, not his campaign manager, so I get to say the other part out loud: **If Chris wins in less than two weeks, he will be the first out gay man ever to serve in the United States Senate.**
Here's how long this has taken: Barney Frank became the first member of Congress to come out voluntarily in 1987. It took another 25 years for an openly gay candidate, Tammy Baldwin, to win a Senate seat. And in the entire history of that chamber, _**not one out gay man has ever served there.**_
Chris could change that. That matters. It matters to Chris and me, and it matters to people all across this country who have never once seen themselves in that room.
**[In 11 days we can make that history real. If this moment means something to you too, will you chip in to help Chris win?](https://substack.com/redirect/1b4028a7-73d1-4bbb-9b68-d6b48fc2a4f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/1b4028a7-73d1-4bbb-9b68-d6b48fc2a4f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
When Chris was growing up in Manchester, he attended one of the biggest public high schools in the state, and as far as he knew, there wasn't a single out student there. No gay-straight alliance. Nobody to look at and think, _that could be me._ He has said he's now living a life he didn't think was possible back then.
He came out in college, returned home, and ran for the State House at age 22 without hiding who he was. New Hampshire embraced him then, and it's embracing him now. Chris likes to point to our state motto, "Live Free or Die." To him it means people here, whatever their politics, want their neighbors to be free to be themselves. I've watched that play out in coffee shops, at town halls, and on front porches across this state.
And Chris has never been quiet about the fight itself. In 2004 his very first speech on the House floor was against a bill to block New Hampshire from recognizing same-sex marriages. He called it what it was. He lost that vote. Five years later New Hampshire legalized marriage equality, six years before it became the law of the land nationwide. In Congress he became co-chair of the Equality Caucus and has championed bills to expand civil rights protections for LGBTQ Americans and to restore benefits for veterans who were discharged just for being who they are.
**I 've never met anyone more patient about the long game or more stubborn about winning it.**
That's why it meant so much to me that the _Times_ wrote about a young organizer who said that in part because of Chris, he came out to his family and friends and found out the people around him love him for exactly who he is.
There are kids in high schools all over this country right now walking the same hallway Chris did, unsure whether there will be a place for them wherever they want to end up. They're watching this race whether anyone tells them to or not. **If Chris wins they 'll see there's no ceiling on what you can achieve based on who you love.**
Somersworth's Mayor Gerding told the _Times_ this is the kind of milestone you'd want to sing from the rooftops. I agree. **So consider this email my rooftop.**
And it couldn't come at a more important moment. Just last week the Vice President mocked a Democratic Senate candidate by falsely suggesting he was gay, as if that were an insult. As Chris put it, cynical attacks on the LGBTQ community have gone mainstream, and a lot of people are scared about where this country is headed. **A win in New Hampshire would be a loud answer.**
Republicans know what's at stake, too: **This race could decide who controls the Senate.** If we win New Hampshire, Democrats can flip the Senate and finally put a check on this administration. If we lose Republicans keep their grip on the majority, and this era of chaos rolls on. And they're spending over $60 million to do it.
**[This race is about more than Chris. It's about the future of our country. So I'm asking you to make a contribution in the final stretch:](https://substack.com/redirect/1b4028a7-73d1-4bbb-9b68-d6b48fc2a4f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/1b4028a7-73d1-4bbb-9b68-d6b48fc2a4f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**On November 3rd we have a chance to take back the Senate majority** _**and**_**make history on the same night.**
I'm so proud of Chris. I'm so proud of New Hampshire. Thank you for standing with us.
Vann Bentley (Chris's husband)

clean_body: A message from Vann, Chris's husband | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more He doesn't dwell on it, but I want you to understand what this means to people. Oct 23 | | | | | | | | | | | It's Vann, Chris's husband. I don't often write to you, but I read something that I wanted to share. The New York Times published a profile of Chris yesterday with the headline: " His Election Could Decide Senate Control. He Could Make History, Too." | | ---|---|--- Both halves of that headline are true. But Chris is only focused on the first one. That's who he is. When the Times asked him about making history, he said he isn't thinking much about it, that he's focused every day on the people of New Hampshire. On the trail it's the same: affordable health care, high prices, corruption in Washington. He means every word. It's one of the many reasons I love him. But I'm his husband, not his campaign manager, so I get to say the other part out loud: If Chris wins in less than two weeks, he will be the first out gay man ever to serve in the United States Senate. Here's how long this has taken: Barney Frank became the first member of Congress to come out voluntarily in 1987. It took another 25 years for an openly gay candidate, Tammy Baldwin, to win a Senate seat. And in the entire history of that chamber, not one out gay man has ever served there. Chris could change that. That matters. It matters to Chris and me, and it matters to people all across this country who have never once seen themselves in that room. When Chris was growing up in Manchester, he attended one of the biggest public high schools in the state, and as far as he knew, there wasn't a single out student there. No gay-straight alliance. Nobody to look at and think, that could be me. He has said he's now living a life he didn't think was possible back then. He came out in college, returned home, and ran for the State House at age 22 without hiding who he was. New Hampshire embraced him then, and it's embracing him now. Chris likes to point to our state motto, "Live Free or Die." To him it means people here, whatever their politics, want their neighbors to be free to be themselves. I've watched that play out in coffee shops, at town halls, and on front porches across this state. And Chris has never been quiet about the fight itself. In 2004 his very first speech on the House floor was against a bill to block New Hampshire from recognizing same-sex marriages. He called it what it was. He lost that vote. Five years later New Hampshire legalized marriage equality, six years before it became the law of the land nationwide. In Congress he became co-chair of the Equality Caucus and has championed bills to expand civil rights protections for LGBTQ Americans and to restore benefits for veterans who were discharged just for being who they are. I 've never met anyone more patient about the long game or more stubborn about winning it. That's why it meant so much to me that the Times wrote about a young organizer who said that in part because of Chris, he came out to his family and friends and found out the people around him love him for exactly who he is. There are kids in high schools all over this country right now walking the same hallway Chris did, unsure whether there will be a place for them wherever they want to end up. They're watching this race whether anyone tells them to or not. If Chris wins they 'll see there's no ceiling on what you can achieve based on who you love. Somersworth's Mayor Gerding told the Times this is the kind of milestone you'd want to sing from the rooftops. I agree. So consider this email my rooftop. And it couldn't come at a more important moment. Just last week the Vice President mocked a Democratic Senate candidate by falsely suggesting he was gay, as if that were an insult. As Chris put it, cynical attacks on the LGBTQ community have gone mainstream, and a lot of people are scared about where this country is headed. A win in New Hampshire would be a loud answer. Republicans know what's at stake, too: This race could decide who controls the Senate. If we win New Hampshire, Democrats can flip the Senate and finally put a check on this administration. If we lose Republicans keep their grip on the majority, and this era of chaos rolls on. And they're spending over $60 million to do it. On November 3rd we have a chance to take back the Senate majority andmake history on the same night. I'm so proud of Chris. I'm so proud of New Hampshire. Thank you for standing with us. Vann Bentley (Chris's husband) | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Chris Pappas PO Box 313, Manchester, NH 03105 ? ?

Trump's endorsement of Max Engling for Indiana Secretary of State."Congratulations to Max Engling on receiving the endorsement of President Donald J. _**The weak department?**_ I enlisted in the Marine Corps right out of high school. I made sergeant, then spent decades in the Army and retired as a Brigadier General. After 9/11, I led infantry soldiers in combat in Afghanistan. In 2014, I took a team into Liberia while Ebola was killing thousands, because that was the mission and somebody had to go. **I never served with a single weak person in 40 years.** Not the young soldiers who walked patrols knowing what could be waiting for them. Not the medics, mechanics, and cooks who kept us alive and moving. Not the military families who held everything together at home while we were gone. So who does Pete Hegseth think he is? **Our armed forces have never been weak. Not under any president or any party. Those men and women were strong long before he got a podium, and they'll be strong long after he's gone.** Northwest Georgia is full of veterans and military families who know that truth. They deserve a representative who will stand up and say it proudly. Right now, Clay Fuller holds this seat, and I haven't heard him say a word. On November 3, I'm asking voters to send someone to Congress who knows what our troops are made of, because I served with them. **We have 29 days left. Every dollar helps us get this message on TV screens, in mailboxes, and on veterans' doors across the district before Election Day. So I am asking: Can you chip in $25 right now to send a veteran to Congress who will stand up to Pete Hegseth?**

clean_body: | | Pete Hegseth stood in front of our service members and said this: "We are no longer the woke department or the weak department." | The weak department? I enlisted in the Marine Corps right out of high school. I made sergeant, then spent decades in the Army and retired as a Brigadier General. After 9/11, I led infantry soldiers in combat in Afghanistan. In 2014, I took a team into Liberia while Ebola was killing thousands, because that was the mission and somebody had to go. I never served with a single weak person in 40 years. Not the young soldiers who walked patrols knowing what could be waiting for them. Not the medics, mechanics, and cooks who kept us alive and moving. Not the military families who held everything together at home while we were gone. So who does Pete Hegseth think he is? Our armed forces have never been weak. Not under any president or any party. Those men and women were strong long before he got a podium, and they'll be strong long after he's gone. Northwest Georgia is full of veterans and military families who know that truth. They deserve a representative who will stand up and say it proudly. Right now, Clay Fuller holds this seat, and I haven't heard him say a word. On November 3, I'm asking voters to send someone to Congress who knows what our troops are made of, because I served with them. We have 29 days left. Every dollar helps us get this message on TV screens, in mailboxes, and on veterans' doors across the district before Election Day. So I am asking: Can you chip in $25 right now to send a veteran to Congress who will stand up to Pete Hegseth? ~~ ~~ Thank you, Ret. # [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=1154%2E127862%2Ey4etjG)
Folks,
I just made one of the toughest calls of this campaign.
Recently, I signed off on an ad plan for the next couple of days: to amplify our campaign’s message in Las Vegas, Reno, and everywhere in between.
I need to be straight with you: **we don't have all the money to pay for it yet.**
At this point in the race, we have to go big or go home. The polls show MAGA Gov. Joe Lombardo and I are locked in a dead heat.
But we’re being heavily outspent over the airwaves, and if this is our last shot to get in front of undecided voters before Lombardo does, I have to go for it.
**[I’m counting on this grassroots team to help fund the final stretch of this race. Can you chip in $5 or any amount today?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261023_4_ak.uVzyGJ&amount=5&refcode=em20261023-1154&t=3&akid=1154%2E127862%2Ey4etjG)**

This is our best chance to flip a governor's seat blue in 2026. I believe we can win, but only if we finish strong.
Thank you,
Aaron

subject: I have to ask you this
body:
A goal we cannot afford to miss
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1739&source=&t=1&akid=4830%2E124072%2EQocSSC) | | | |

Hey Peter, it’s Roy. I’m sorry to be direct like this, but I have to ask you to [**_chip in $5 to my campaign right now._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1739&amount=5&t=8&akid=4830%2E124072%2EQocSSC)
President Trump and JD Vance were back in North Carolina earlier this week for a MAGA rally with my opponent Michael Whatley – and President Trump promised to return _again_ next week. So my team and I set a critical daily fundraising goal to make sure we have the resources to fight back and reach every last voter before Election Day. As it stands, we’re falling short. This is a goal we cannot afford to miss.
The GOP has already spent tens of millions to defeat me, and we need the resources to keep pace in this final stretch. If we lose here, Democrats lose our chance at flipping the Senate.
Will you please chip in any amount today to help us win? Not tomorrow, not the next day. _Today, Peter._
Here’s the link one more time: [**_https:/ /secure.actblue.com/donate_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1739&amount=5&t=9&akid=4830%2E124072%2EQocSSC)
Thank you so much,
Roy
| |

[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1739&t=2&akid=4830%2E124072%2EQocSSC)
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

[INSIDE JW]

VICTORY: COURT ORDERS CIA TO BEGIN PRODUCING JANUARY 6 RECORDS

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=39009&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj05WllqX0g4M2hhRSZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=]&H=aabb201075dbd0b8878c1470071ed74cf0ffc762bdaa9ba1afdd988545708a67

We’ve moved a step closer in our pursuit of the truth about January
6.

A federal court ordered
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=38980&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtY2lhLWo2LXJvbGxpbmctcHJvZHVjdGlvbnMtb3JkZXItMDIxNzIvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==]&H=4f3b0e70cbbedb418a3f4bb732bc449b02b0d4f383959b7e017d120227ac4b7f
the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) to begin producing records by
November 16, 2026, in response to our Freedom of Information Act
(FOIA) lawsuit seeking information about CIA personnel and support at
the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021.

We filed the July 2024 lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=33154&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvamFudWFyeS02LTIwMjEtcHJvdGVzdHMvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==]&H=7bb512343050f4a3656cce1ed6020c8a2ed7dea199b5deb42577db46d35d6507 after the CIA
failed to respond to a March 2024 FOIA request asking the agency to
produce records concerning the January 6, 2021, events, including
shots fired and a person shot inside the U.S. Capitol, requests for
CIA assistance, bomb technicians and bomb-detection dogs deployed or
placed on standby, and after-action reports documenting the events
(_Judicial Watch v. Central Intelligence Agency_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=33122&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtY2lhLWo2LXNob3RzLWJvbWItdGVjaC1jb21wbGFpbnQtMDIxNzIvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==]&H=8b84df049ab10bfd098a3bb94da23b58349406df05f8804a872189b65f146c84
(No. 1:24-cv-02172)).

In March 2024, we received 88 pages
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=31656&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvY2lhLWJvbWItdGVjaHMtamFudWFyeS02Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=]&H=9e0816de04e53527e2468ddc406a1d27f37eedb88eb3218f02166fdee9037619 of Bureau of
Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) records from the
Department of Justice in a FOIA lawsuit that show the CIA deployed
personnel to Washington, DC on January 6, 2021.

The records include a series of text messages under the heading
“January 7 Intel Chain
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=31595&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWF0Zi1qYW4tNi1wcm9kLTEtMDE2MDgtcGdzLTQ5LTg4L13igJ0/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&H=5faf2a212bc0ca95dd7ac16ec3d4df308f4343310937997df8c33a5040cf95d0
in which two separate references to participation by the CIA are made.
One states
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=31596&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWF0Zi1qYW4tNi1wcm9kLTEtMDE2MDgtcGctNjUvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==]&H=0e772c1b3ab93f5c23a726206e94e8cc610a9c69c67b05cea417433c17fd1fc5
that “two CIA bomb techs” are assisting with “a pipe bomb scene
on New Jersey and D ST SE.” Another record references “several CIA
dog teams on standby
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=31597&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWF0Zi1qYW4tNi1wcm9kLTEtMDE2MDgtcGctNzIvXS7igJ0/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&H=43532271ab074e118c4fea4443f425a7d12be93530011fde38e2bb49c6d38820

In the October 15, 2026, minute order
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=38980&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtY2lhLWo2LXJvbGxpbmctcHJvZHVjdGlvbnMtb3JkZXItMDIxNzIvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==],&H=8ddd506da42b3b646c634eec29f56f5b283279ccaf5b93406c615e49e581c9a4 U.S.
District Judge Jia M. Cobb directed the CIA to begin rolling interim
productions of responsive records by November 16, rejecting the
agency’s refusal to provide records next year:

> MINUTE ORDER re [24] Notice: Defendant received Plaintiff’s
> request in March 2024, ECF 1 ¶ 8, and, at one point, represented
> that it “anticipated beginning rolling productions no later than
> April 2025,” ECF 23 at 2. Defendant did not meet that anticipated
> deadline after identifying additional necessary searches. ECF 23 at
> 2. The Court’s September 24, 2026 minute order directed Defendant
> to identify a date certain on which it would begin rolling interim
> productions of responsive records. Defendant’s [24] notice
> indicated that it will not process rolling productions and will
> instead produce non-exempt responsive material by May 24, 2027.
> Because Defendant did not provide a date certain to begin rolling
> productions as the Court ordered, and has offered no explanation for
> its position, the Court will set a date that it finds reasonable
> based on the record. Accordingly, the Court ORDERS Defendant to
> begin rolling interim productions of responsive records by November
> 16, 2026. Signed by Judge Jia M. Cobb on October 15, 2026. (lcjmc1)

We are obviously pleased that the court clapped back against the
CIA’s utter contempt for the American people’s right to know what
it was up to at the U.S. Capitol on January 6. We look forward to
finally getting documents next month – after years of cover-up.

We have pursued details of January 6 on several fronts.

In July 2026, we forced the release
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=38173&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvamFudWFyeS02LWJvZHljYW0tdmlkZW9zLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=]&H=2fe0bf168e13a15f29df95dc506e5026189bbee7259a072a391f1e6a38f37cb5 of over
1,000 hours of Washington, DC, Metropolitan Police Department
body-worn camera footage from the January 6, 2021, U.S. Capitol event.

In April 2026, we filed
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=35132&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvaXJzLXRhcmdldGluZy1vZi1qYW51YXJ5LTYtcHJvdGVzdGVycy8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE]&H=a8a3385c99636ccd810da588a7397cd9e65611f44ae7cc11b00b8e70ab4e3831
a FOIA lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=35132&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvaXJzLXRhcmdldGluZy1vZi1qYW51YXJ5LTYtcHJvdGVzdGVycy8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE]&H=a8a3385c99636ccd810da588a7397cd9e65611f44ae7cc11b00b8e70ab4e3831
against the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to obtain records related
to possible improper targeting of January 6, 2021, Capitol protesters,
their supporters, and related nonprofits.

In July 2025, we sued
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=36077&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvbGFzdC1taW51dGUtajYtdGFyZ2V0aW5nLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=]&H=c260cfdcebfb3d81e69172efc57959b829835b2beb64c48f9da7354f2cebadd6 the U.S.
Department of Justice for records on accelerated January 6
prosecutions after Donald Trump was elected president in November
2024.

In June 2025, we obtained
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=35379&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvNC05NzUtbWlsbGlvbi1zZXR0bGVtZW50LW9mLWFzaGxpLWJhYmJpdHQvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==]&H=96188e4e65688362fdd98da812c6142d95c61fe1d96041b6fd2f7b5ae927aa70
a $4.975 million settlement
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=35357&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2VzdGF0ZS1vZi1hc2hsaS1iYWJiaXR0LWV0LWFsLXYtdS1zLWEtc2V0dGxlbWVudC0wMDAzMy0wMTcwMS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE]&H=ff5994d0c48db4192a45b257a3a75ad0d9da9aeb0ba7b56e02ab98f3322c6e79
in the wrongful death lawsuit against the U.S. Government filed on
behalf of the family of Ashli Babbitt, the U.S. Air Force veteran who
was shot and killed [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=35358&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dS5iZS91aU1zUnZObjkxZz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=]&H=0d87b5111743b2bcf353e9a68e63f25bca51ca6b99082f704720188db4211eb9 inside the U.S.
Capitol by then-Capitol Police Lt. Michael Byrd on January 6, 2021.
Ashli Babbitt was the only January 6 homicide victim.

In October 2023, we received the declaration
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=30448&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvamFudWFyeS02Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=]&H=73cbc8360f846f170bd4409af4e9478c366cd0fac32ccaaf26fdd46cc2032cad of James W. Joyce, senior
counsel in the Office of the General Counsel for the Capitol Police,
in which he describes emails among senior officials of the United
States Capitol Police (USCP) in January 2021 that show warnings of
possible January 6 protests that could lead to serious disruptions at
the U.S. Capitol.

JUDICIAL WATCH SUES FOR FBI’S ‘ROSETTA STONE’ REPORT ON
TRUMP-RUSSIA PROBE

We are suing the U.S. Department of Justice for a 2021 FBI report on
Operation Crossfire Hurricane, the controversial investigation into
alleged 2016 Trump campaign ties to Russia.

We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=38990&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWNyb3NzZmlyZS1odXJyaWNhbmUtY29tcGxhaW50LTAzNjAzLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=]&H=9816e9a6940030dc5efac04a1f162abe44db53dc070d35bd6769d2b13654ae56
against the Justice Department for a 2021 investigative report by the
FBI’s Office of Professional Responsibility (OPR) concerning
Operation Crossfire Hurricane, the FBI’s investigation into alleged
links between the 2016 Trump presidential campaign and Russia
(_Judicial Watch, Inc. v. U.S. Department of Justice_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=38990&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWNyb3NzZmlyZS1odXJyaWNhbmUtY29tcGxhaW50LTAzNjAzLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=]&H=9816e9a6940030dc5efac04a1f162abe44db53dc070d35bd6769d2b13654ae56
(1:26-cv-03603)).

We sued after the FBI failed to respond to an August 7, 2026, FOIA
request for the following records:

> A copy of the investigative report produced by the FBI’s Office of
> Professional Responsibility in 2021 relating to Operation Crossfire
> Hurricane, reportedly consisting of approximately 400 pages, plus
> approximately 7,000 pages of attachments, as more fully described at
> https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=38992&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly9yLnpyeS5uZXQvMjAyNi8wOC9pcy1mYmktaGlkaW5nLXRoZS00MDAtcGFnZS1yb3NldHRhLXN0b25lLXRoYXQtY291bGQtc2VhbC1qb2huLWJyZW5uYW5zLWZhdGUvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=9c18fa06342911e737500ffa39cd40791b308b4a6d0dfce3326ffbf180dbd228
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=38992&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly9yLnpyeS5uZXQvMjAyNi8wOC9pcy1mYmktaGlkaW5nLXRoZS00MDAtcGFnZS1yb3NldHRhLXN0b25lLXRoYXQtY291bGQtc2VhbC1qb2huLWJyZW5uYW5zLWZhdGUvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==]&H=87e97414edaf91d7d499d602dcd21d434651b18c982e417df8472f129909728d

In August 2026 investigative journalist Paul Sperry reported
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86176&L=38993&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9wYXVsc3BlcnJ5Xy9zdGF0dXMvMjA4NTIwNzQ2ODgyNTUzNDgyNj91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=]&H=e74640dc3bf76624927be4671201724fa7261ba86e7cdb8725e6456367ae5d00 that sources
told him the FBI was withholding from declassification a 2021 Office
of Professional Responsibility report examining Crossfire Hurricane.
According to Sperry, the report contains approximately 400 pages and

Central Intelligence Agency [ (No. 1:24-cv-02172)). In March 2024, we received 88 pages [ of Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) records from the Department of Justice in a FOIA lawsuit that show the CIA deployed personnel to Washington, DC on January 6, 2021. The records include a series of text messages under the heading “January 7 Intel Chain [ in which two separate references to participation by the CIA are made. Cobb directed the CIA to begin rolling interim productions of responsive records by November 16, rejecting the agency’s refusal to provide records next year: MINUTE ORDER re [24] Notice: Defendant received Plaintiff’s request in March 2024, ECF 1 ¶ 8, and, at one point, represented that it “anticipated beginning rolling productions no later than April 2025,” ECF 23 at 2. In September 2019 we released State Department records [ revealing that Steele had an extensive and close working relationship dating back to May of 2014 with high-ranking Obama State Department officials including Jonathan Winer and Victoria Nuland. In August 2019 we obtained “302” report material [ from 2016 FBI interviews of Associate Deputy U.S. Attorney Bruce Ohr, who was removed from his position in December 2017. (A Form 302 is used by FBI agents to memorialize interviews they undertake during an investigation.) In a November 22, 2016, interview, Ohr said that “reporting on Trump’s ties to Russia were going to the Clinton Campaign, Jon Winer at the U.S. State Department and the FBI.” In a late September 2016 interview, Ohr described a person (likely Christopher Steele) as “desperate that Donald Trump not get elected and was passionate about him not being the U.S. President.” A report states that “Ohr knew that [Fusion GPS’s] Glen Simpson and others were talking to Victoria Nuland at the U.S. State Department.” In July 2019 we obtained records [ revealing a September 2016 email exchange between then-Assistant Secretary of State Victoria Nuland and Special Coordinator for Libya Jonathan Winer, a close associate of dossier author Christopher Steele, discussing a “face-to-face” meeting on a “Russian matter.” In August 2018 the Justice Department admitted in a Judicial Watch FOIA lawsuit court filing that the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court held no hearings [ on the FISA spy warrant applications targeting Carter Page, a former Trump campaign part-time advisor who was the subject of four controversial FISA warrants. U.S. TAKES ‘FEW ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS’ ON HIGH RISK VISA OVERSTAYS We know our southern border was wide open under the Biden administration, but it turns out that our visa program is also seriously flawed. Our Corruption Chronicles blog has the details [ As if it weren’t bad enough that the U.S. government has long compromised national security by losing track of foreigners—like several of the 9/11 terrorists—who overstay their visa, in many cases it fails to take enforcement actions on solid leads of those who may pose a threat to the country. This is a huge problem because every year tens of millions of foreign nationals receive nonimmigrant visas to enter the U.S. for tourism, business or study and hundreds of thousands stay beyond their authorized period of admission annually, violating the terms of the visa which the feds categorize as overstays. The State Department issues the visas, and a new federal probe [ reveals that from fiscal year 2021 to 2024, the agency distributed more than 31 million. Incredibly, under the Biden administration’s lax rules over 12 million were granted without required vetting of in-person interviews or fingerprint collection, putting the country at risk by approving certain visa holders who represent national security or safety threats. Adding insult to injury, federal authorities took few enforcement actions even when they had “targeted leads” concerning foreigners who overstayed their visa, according to the recently published investigation conducted by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Inspector General. “As a result, foreign nationals who potentially posed threats to the United States remained at large despite their illegal status,” the watchdog confirms. The lapse is like a punch in the gut for the American public two and a half decades after Islamic terrorists exploited this inefficient system for tracking foreigners who overstay visas to remain in the country. It allowed the 9/11 hijackers to live in the U.S., plan, and conduct the deadliest terrorist attack on American soil, killing nearly 3,000 people. After the attacks Congress created a system to track the entry and exit of foreign nationals by using electronically scanned fingerprints and photographs. It was called the U.S. Visitor and Immigration Status Indicator Technology (US VISIT), and it was seriously flawed even though the government invested around a billion dollars over several years to get it going. It never worked properly, however. Now we find out that even when visa overstays are credibly identified as a possible threat to the nation, federal authorities do not act. As unbelievable as this may seem, the recently published audit reveals that in the four fiscal years examined Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) received over 3 million overstay leads of which it categorized 104,049 as potential national security and public safety concerns. Even the highest priority visa overstay led investigations representing only the maximum risk led to few arrests, DHS investigators found. During the four years analyzed Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) identified 1,769 so-called “Priority 1” leads and conducted 84 probes that resulted in just two arrests. The number of foreigners who overstay their visa and remain unmonitored inside the country has grown significantly in the quarter century since Al Qaeda operatives executed the deadliest terrorist attack in American history. Years ago, the investigative arm of Congress, the Government Accountability Office (GAO) found [ that nearly half of the nation’s illegal aliens entered the U.S. legally and overstayed their visa undetected. Other federal investigations have revealed that the U.S. has failed to remove millions with expired visas, including DHS losing track of hundreds of dangerous foreigners that “could pose a national security or public safety concerns.” Every year the government fails to catch hundreds of thousands of foreign nationals who overstay their visa. In fiscal year 2015 it was more than half a million [ including thousands from terrorist nations like Pakistan, Iraq, Yemen, Libya, and Syria. A few years later the number of overstays increased to 702,000 [ Among them was a Portuguese man charged in the gruesome kidnap and murder of a young woman whose body was found bound in a suitcase on a Connecticut street. name: Roy Cooper
subject: Just 10 days
body:
We can’t take our foot off the gas until we cross the checkered line.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1743&source=&t=1&akid=4863%2E124072%2EYfXjQr) | | | |
---
Peter,
We’re just 10 days out from the most important midterm election of our lifetimes.
As of Wednesday, more than one million North Carolinians have already cast their ballots – and time’s running out to reach the 7% of persuadable voters who’ll decide the outcome of this race.
**So if you’ve been waiting to make your first donation to my U.S. Senate campaign, there’s no better time than today.[_We need to raise another $500,000 by tomorrow at midnight to power our final get-out-the-vote push, so will you please chip in right away?_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1743&amount=5&t=8&akid=4863%2E124072%2EYfXjQr)**
It’s been nearly 20 years since NC sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate. Not only do experts say our campaign is the best chance to change that – there’s _no way_ we take back Senate control without flipping this seat on Nov. 3.
Until then, we’re racing to connect with as many North Carolinians as we can. I’m traveling all across the state for our “Make Stuff Cost Less” tour, and our volunteers are knocking doors and calling phones statewide to ensure folks have a plan to vote.
But I’m taking a moment to reach out to you now because this is a people-powered campaign. Every ad we run, every event we hold and every door we knock on is funded by folks like you.
We can’t take our foot off the gas until we cross the checkered line on election night **– so it’s all the more urgent that I can count on you today.**
[**_Please, Peter: Click here now to make your first contribution to our campaign’s GOTV goal today. Even $5 will make a difference for our voter outreach efforts in the final week and a half of this must-win race._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1743&amount=5&t=9&akid=4863%2E124072%2EYfXjQr)

subject: Donald Trump is suing
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
DC people want to play partisan games while I am fighting for Alaska’s future.
It's Mary Peltola. I want you to hear this from me:
The Trump Administration is suing preemptively to try to keep Dan Sullivan in power because they're terrified he’ll lose this race in 10 days.
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20261024-1.1ZdW9n&refcode=em20261024-4051&t=1&akid=4051%2E21716%2E85UZqH)
Look, I’m not used to this Lower 48 hyperpartisan BS.
It’s not how we do things in Alaska. Where I’m from in the Bush, there’s a big premium on respect. We depend on each other too much to burn bridges over political differences.
But if they think I won’t fight back when DC people try to play partisan games with our future, they’ve got another thing coming.
I’m running to take on the rigged DC system that’s hurting all of us, and I won’t let this sham stop me.
But the truth is, the only way we’re going to make sure every single Alaskan’s voice is heard over the next 10 days is together. That's why I need all hands on deck right now to respond.
[**If you’re with me, please split a $5 contribution between my campaign and Sarah McBride. With lots of people like you stepping up, we can overcome any obstacle and take this fight for fish, family, freedom to DC.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20261024-1.1ZdW9n&refcode=em20261024-4051&amount=5&t=2&akid=4051%2E21716%2E85UZqH)
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20261024-1.1ZdW9n&amount=5&refcode=em20261024-4051&t=21&akid=4051%2E21716%2E85UZqH)**
I’m the underdog in this battle against the DC establishment, so I’m counting on a huge grassroots effort to fight back in this final stretch.
We need to send a strong message to everyone watching that we won’t let their meddling stop us. So thank you for coming together to help me do just that.
Together,
Mary

[ https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261024-1-ak&t=1027&akid=1123%2E1347274%2E5kQK_u ]'New York Times: In Texas, Talarico Inspires a Recurring Blue-Tinted
Dream In the go-big-or-go-home collective consciousness of Texas, no
ambition is deemed too reckless, no daydream too wild. Save perhaps one.
It is the idea, fantastical to many as it is irresistible to others, that
the Democrats will win a statewide race in Texas for the first time in 32
years. According to the latest New York Times/Siena University poll of the
race for U.S. Senate, James Talarico, a 37-year-old state legislator seen
by national Democrats as one of the breakout stars of this cycle, is ahead
of his Republican rival, Ken Paxton, the state’s scandal-plagued attorney
general, by six points. The poll was conducted from Sept. 21 to Sept. 30.
A survey from mid-September, the ReconMR/Siena Research Institute poll,
also showed the Democratic gubernatorial candidate, Gina Hinojosa, four
points ahead of the three-term G.O.P. incumbent, Greg Abbott, the most
dominant political figure in Texas. Cue the fluttering heartbeats. Cue, as
well, the eye-rolls. Given how thoroughly Republicans have dominated the
state, and how the hopes of Democrats have repeatedly crashed, some Texas
pollsters remain skeptical. “At some point, you do get conditioned by all
that’s happened in the past,” said James Henson, the director of the
University of Texas at Austin’s Texas Politics Project. “I mean, you look
at the trends and you have to admit that something’s going on. But you
still don’t want to believe your lying eyes, because you’ve been burned
for so long.” Mr. Henson was referring to the perennial spectacle of
much-ballyhooed Texas Democratic aspirants face-planting against the Lone
Star State’s red wall. First came Tony Sanchez Jr., the swaggering and
self-funding Laredo oilman whom Gov. Rick Perry dispatched in 2002 by an
18-point margin. Next was the state senator Wendy Davis, who attracted
worldwide attention for her filibuster in the Texas Legislature against an
anti-abortion measure but whom Mr. Abbott demolished by 20 points in 2014.
Finally, the El Paso congressman Beto O’Rourke came up 2.6 points short of
defeating Senator Ted Cruz in 2018 but then suffered a 10-point loss to
Mr. Abbott four years later. Even with the awareness of such humiliations,
Democrats find themselves maintaining that 2026 could, at long last, be
the year. President Trump’s deep unpopularity and the prospect of a blue
wave could, they insist, extend into the state he won by nearly 14 points
in 2024. According to a September survey conducted by Texas Southern
University, Mr. Trump is seven points underwater in Texas. Mr. Talarico
has run an energetic and well-financed campaign, while Mr. Paxton has
staged far fewer public events and has had to rely on outside groups to
fund an attack-ad blitzkrieg against his Democratic opponent. Mr. Abbott,
meanwhile, has outspent Ms. Hinojosa by a 10-to-one ratio, yet has been
unable to build an insurmountable lead. “People have vastly underestimated
Gina,” said Ms. Davis, now a political consultant and a senior adviser to
Planned Parenthood Texas Votes, an advocacy organization. “Dollar for
dollar, she’s running the best statewide campaign we’ve ever seen.” Such
optimism stands in defiance of the political axiom that Texas is where
idealistic Democrats go to be mugged by reality. The party’s demise there
is not a product of ill fortune, Mr. Henson said. “Governor Abbott has
built an impressive election machine that has benefited state-level
Republicans again and again for a decade and a half,” he said. “And the
Democratic machinery here is almost nonexistent.” A ‘Hollowing-Out’ I have
written about the politics of my native state at regular intervals for
more than three decades. After watching the Democrats’ century-long rule
in Texas come to a decisive end with Gov. Ann Richards’s loss to George W.
Bush in 1994, I saw the party descend into atrophy in which failure begot
more failure. “The 30-year drought has done a lot of things,” said Luke
Warford, the chairman of the Travis County Democratic Party and the
founder of the Agave Democratic Infrastructure Fund. “It’s kept donors on
the sidelines, which makes a lot of potentially good candidates not run
because there’s no belief they can win. And it also makes a lot of really
talented staff leave to find better-paying work in true battleground
states.” The Democratic Party has no counterpart to Mr. Abbott, and hasn’t
since 1993, when Senator Lloyd Bentsen moved to Washington to join
President Bill Clinton’s cabinet. Its weaknesses are even more glaring
farther down the hierarchy. In recent elections, as many as one-third of
state races have gone uncontested by Democrats. One-fifth of the party’s
county chairs and two-thirds of its precinct chairs have been left
unfilled. Until last year, the state party had a negative operating
budget. As the veteran Democratic consultant Matt Angle observed, “There’s
been a hollowing-out of the party.” Still, those of us who recall the
satisfied sense of invincibility among Texas Democrats after roughly a
century of one-party rule have detected similar signs of overconfidence
among the state’s ruling party. The party’s rightward tilt, increasingly
forceful with each legislative session, reached its apotheosis in March,
with Mr. Paxton’s primary victory over the more moderate Republican
four-term incumbent, Senator John Cornyn. Mr. Paxton, a close ally of Mr.
Trump’s, was impeached by the Republican-controlled State House (and later
acquitted by the State Senate) in 2023 over allegations that included
bribery. He was also accused by his wife of adultery. Mr. Trump endorsed
him anyway, all but guaranteeing his landslide primary triumph over Mr.
Cornyn but in the process testing the allegiance of center-right Texans.
In similar fashion, the Texas G.O.P. is in danger of losing many Latino
voters who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024 after years of siding with
Democrats. “We adopted a lazy way of campaigning that bit us on the ass,
and we’ve learned from that,” Mr. O’Rourke said. “Now it’s the Republicans
who’ve gotten really lazy and complacent and comfortable.” Signs of
Republican Overreach Simply spending one week driving through the vastness
of Texas, as I did in September, is all it takes to appreciate an underdog
party’s uphill battle. The state’s 32 million residents are spread across
20 media markets, many of them distinct ecosystems, from the urban colossi
of Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex to the oil patch of the
Texas Panhandle to the Latino-dominated borderlands of the Rio Grande
Valley. “When national donors are deciding where to invest, they look at a
place like Iowa, where $5 million can fully fund a race,” said Katherine
Fischer, the director of the Texas Majority PAC, which was established by
the liberal philanthropist Soros family. “That’s why Texas is always at
the bottom of their list. It’s just so damned big.” Reaching so many
markets presents a daunting challenge for an upstart candidate like Ms.
Hinojosa, a state representative from the border city of Brownsville.
“There’s still 20 percent of the electorate that doesn’t know who I am,”
she said in an interview in mid-September. To date, Ms. Hinojosa’s
campaign has said that it has raised about $20 million. For his part, Mr.
Talarico spent about $30 million earlier this year to introduce himself
statewide as a man of Christian faith and a member of the Texas House with
a record of supporting bipartisan legislation. Since that time, however,
Mr. Paxton and his associates have invested more than $100 million in an
effort to redefine his opponent as “radical” and “weird,” with ads that
quote from remarks Mr. Talarico made several years ago (and later
renounced) suggesting that “God is nonbinary” and that there are six
biological sexes. Mr. Paxton and his allies have at times questioned Mr.
Talarico’s manhood and even his Christianity, an effort to jolt the
sensibilities of a state prone to mythologizing godly and masculine
archetypes. “How they’re negatively defining Talarico is kind of a
bank-shot way of saying that he’s not a true Texas conservative,” Mr.
Henson said. Whether money can overwhelm conditions on the ground is the
riddle looming over the Texas races. In the border city of Laredo, which
Mr. Trump won in 2024 — the first time a Republican had done so in over a
century — signs of buyer’s remorse are evident. Arrests by Immigration and
Customs Enforcement agents in Laredo were higher in July than in any other
American city. Mr. Trump’s erratic trade policies have further created
instability at the city’s port of entry. While acknowledging the economic
concerns that many border residents share, Adrian Zapata, a business
executive in the health industry who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, said in
an interview that the negative ads against Mr. Talarico were resonating
with some of his family members. “They see Talarico as an ultraliberal,”
he said. “They’re done with the ‘they/them.’ They’re going to vote for
Paxton just because of that.” As for Mr. Zapata, “I’m not ready to vote
for Talarico,” he said. “But I don’t like Paxton. He’s never done anything
for South Texas, and his personal and business dealings have hurt him a
lot with folks down here.” There is a similarly muddled electoral picture
in the cattle country of deep West Texas adjacent to Big Bend National
Park. Mr. Trump and Mr. Abbott have aggressively championed a border wall
and artificial intelligence data centers, both of which threaten to
disrupt the region’s pastoral ethos. A coalition of more than 200
landowners has sued the federal government over the border wall, while
other residents have circulated a petition to protest the construction of
a new data center near Fort Stockton. George Johnson, a cattle feed
operator in Alpine, waved off such concerns, saying: “Folks worrying about
data centers were also worried when the internet got started. It’s
Talarico who scares me to death, him and all that socialist talk.” Others
in this largely conservative region harbor the view that Republicans have
failed to make good on their promises. Thaddeus Cleveland, the Republican
sheriff of Terrell County, said that both he and his county had voted for
Mr. Trump in 2024, but added, “Everything he campaigned on, we’re seeing
the opposite of, like going to war.” Sheriff Cleveland predicted that the
negative campaign ads by the Republicans would not factor as significantly
into the votes of his neighbors as “the price of groceries and gas, which
are compounded here because we’re so far from everywhere else.” But it is
in purple Tarrant County, dominated by Fort Worth, where the party could
pay the price for having potentially overestimated its mandate from the
voters. Conservative leaders have cut funds for nonprofits that aid
at-risk children, subjected school library books to right-wing litmus
tests and eliminated free bus rides to polling stations in poor
neighborhoods. “The far-right leaders here have implemented Project 2025
on a county level,” said Alisa Simmons, a Democrat and county commissioner
who is running to unseat the conservative county judge, Tim O’Hare. In an
early sign this year that area Republicans may be out of step with Tarrant
County’s constituents, a Democratic aviation machinist and union leader,
Taylor Rehmet, defeated Leigh Wambsganss, a well-funded Republican
Christian activist who led the conservative takeover of several metroplex
school boards. He won by 14 points in a January special election for a
State Senate seat covering a region that Mr. Trump won by 17 points in
2024. A ‘Gradualist’ Theory Which party prevails in Texas is a complicated
riddle. Historically a low-turnout state — it ranked second to last in the
2024 election, ahead of only Arkansas — Texas held a primary in March that
saw nearly one in four voters showing up to the polls, a modern record for
midterm participation, with Democrats slightly outpacing Republicans. A
few factors could conspire to thwart a blue wave in Texas. As of 2020,
straight-ticket voting is no longer possible in the state, which could
impact the mostly Democratic urban counties where that practice has
frequently been used by voters in past elections. Texas is one of only
eight states that lack universal online registration, while voting by mail
is also highly restricted. In January, Mr. Abbott turned over the state’s
list of approximately 18.7 million registered voters to the Trump
administration, and 1.2 million of them have subsequently been put on the
“suspense list” because their addresses have not been verified. The recent
shuttering of nearly one-third of Tarrant County’s polling sites by its
Republican-controlled county commission is particularly worrisome for
Democrats. “The reason we’ve lost these statewide races in the past is
because we’ve never gotten enough out of Tarrant County to overcome the
margins in rural Texas,” Ms. Davis said of the turnout. “If we don’t get
it to 53 or 54 percent this November, it’s game over. James and Gina can’t
win.” But the state’s Republicans have reasons of their own to be fretful.
Partly because of the recruitment efforts of the Texas Majority PAC and
Blueprint Texas, a down-ballot candidate support organization co-founded
by Ms. Davis earlier this year, the Democrats are fielding a full slate in
all 150 state races for the first time in a half-century. Though many of
these aspirants face long odds, their presence on the ballot could
energize the Democrats in predominantly conservative regions who have not
bothered to turn out in the past. “If we win on Nov. 3, most of those
names running down-ballot in really tough areas like East Texas and the
Hill Country and the Panhandle will be responsible,” Mr. O’Rourke said.
Mr. Henson added that while he remained skeptical about Democratic
enthusiasm being sufficient to carry the day for Mr. Talarico, he also
doubted that a last-minute avalanche of negative ads would prove decisive
for Mr. Paxton. “At a certain point, there’s diminishing impact once you
get past an absurd level of spending,” he said. Rather than project a
winner in November, Mr. Henson said he felt more comfortable embracing a
“gradualist” theory, one in which Texas does not become blue overnight,
but instead competitive. “Even if Talarico loses by a Beto-like margin,”
he said, “the next cycle is a presidential election, where Trump likely
won’t be popular and Democratic turnout will be higher. So there are
reasons for Texas Democrats to be optimistic.”'

Its weaknesses are even more glaring farther down the hierarchy. In recent elections, as many as one-third of state races have gone uncontested by Democrats. One-fifth of the party’s county chairs and two-thirds of its precinct chairs have been left unfilled. Until last year, the state party had a negative operating budget. As the veteran Democratic consultant Matt Angle observed, “There’s been a hollowing-out of the party.” Still, those of us who recall the satisfied sense of invincibility among Texas Democrats after roughly a century of one-party rule have detected similar signs of overconfidence among the state’s ruling party. The party’s rightward tilt, increasingly forceful with each legislative session, reached its apotheosis in March, with Mr. Paxton’s primary victory over the more moderate Republican four-term incumbent, Senator John Cornyn. Mr. Paxton, a close ally of Mr. Trump’s, was impeached by the Republican-controlled State House (and later acquitted by the State Senate) in 2023 over allegations that included bribery. He was also accused by his wife of adultery. Mr. Trump endorsed him anyway, all but guaranteeing his landslide primary triumph over Mr. Cornyn but in the process testing the allegiance of center-right Texans. In similar fashion, the Texas G.O.P. is in danger of losing many Latino voters who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024 after years of siding with Democrats. “We adopted a lazy way of campaigning that bit us on the ass, and we’ve learned from that,” Mr. O’Rourke said. “Now it’s the Republicans who’ve gotten really lazy and complacent and comfortable.” Signs of Republican Overreach Simply spending one week driving through the vastness of Texas, as I did in September, is all it takes to appreciate an underdog party’s uphill battle. The state’s 32 million residents are spread across 20 media markets, many of them distinct ecosystems, from the urban colossi of Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex to the oil patch of the Texas Panhandle to the Latino-dominated borderlands of the Rio Grande Valley. “When national donors are deciding where to invest, they look at a place like Iowa, where $5 million can fully fund a race,” said Katherine Fischer, the director of the Texas Majority PAC, which was established by the liberal philanthropist Soros family. “That’s why Texas is always at the bottom of their list. It’s just so damned big.” Reaching so many markets presents a daunting challenge for an upstart candidate like Ms. Hinojosa, a state representative from the border city of Brownsville. “There’s still 20 percent of the electorate that doesn’t know who I am,” she said in an interview in mid-September. To date, Ms. Hinojosa’s campaign has said that it has raised about $20 million. For his part, Mr. Talarico spent about $30 million earlier this year to introduce himself statewide as a man of Christian faith and a member of the Texas House with a record of supporting bipartisan legislation. Since that time, however, Mr. Paxton and his associates have invested more than $100 million in an effort to redefine his opponent as “radical” and “weird,” with ads that quote from remarks Mr. Talarico made several years ago (and later renounced) suggesting that “God is nonbinary” and that there are six biological sexes. Mr. Paxton and his allies have at times questioned Mr. Talarico’s manhood and even his Christianity, an effort to jolt the sensibilities of a state prone to mythologizing godly and masculine archetypes. “How they’re negatively defining Talarico is kind of a bank-shot way of saying that he’s not a true Texas conservative,” Mr. Henson said. Whether money can overwhelm conditions on the ground is the riddle looming over the Texas races. In the border city of Laredo, which Mr. Trump won in 2024 — the first time a Republican had done so in over a century — signs of buyer’s remorse are evident. Arrests by Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents in Laredo were higher in July than in any other American city. Mr. Trump’s erratic trade policies have further created instability at the city’s port of entry. While acknowledging the economic concerns that many border residents share, Adrian Zapata, a business executive in the health industry who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, said in an interview that the negative ads against Mr. Talarico were resonating with some of his family members. “They see Talarico as an ultraliberal,” he said. “They’re done with the ‘they/them.’ They’re going to vote for Paxton just because of that.” As for Mr. Zapata, “I’m not ready to vote for Talarico,” he said. “But I don’t like Paxton. He’s never done anything for South Texas, and his personal and business dealings have hurt him a lot with folks down here.” There is a similarly muddled electoral picture in the cattle country of deep West Texas adjacent to Big Bend National Park. Mr. Trump and Mr. Abbott have aggressively championed a border wall and artificial intelligence data centers, both of which threaten to disrupt the region’s pastoral ethos. A coalition of more than 200 landowners has sued the federal government over the border wall, while other residents have circulated a petition to protest the construction of a new data center near Fort Stockton. George Johnson, a cattle feed operator in Alpine, waved off such concerns, saying: “Folks worrying about data centers were also worried when the internet got started. It’s Talarico who scares me to death, him and all that socialist talk.” Others in this largely conservative region harbor the view that Republicans have failed to make good on their promises. Thaddeus Cleveland, the Republican sheriff of Terrell County, said that both he and his county had voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, but added, “Everything he campaigned on, we’re seeing the opposite of, like going to war.” Sheriff Cleveland predicted that the negative campaign ads by the Republicans would not factor as significantly into the votes of his neighbors as “the price of groceries and gas, which are compounded here because we’re so far from everywhere else.” But it is in purple Tarrant County, dominated by Fort Worth, where the party could pay the price for having potentially overestimated its mandate from the voters. Conservative leaders have cut funds for nonprofits that aid at-risk children, subjected school library books to right-wing litmus tests and eliminated free bus rides to polling stations in poor neighborhoods. “The far-right leaders here have implemented Project 2025 on a county level,” said Alisa Simmons, a Democrat and county commissioner who is running to unseat the conservative county judge, Tim O’Hare. In an early sign this year that area Republicans may be out of step with Tarrant County’s constituents, a Democratic aviation machinist and union leader, Taylor Rehmet, defeated Leigh Wambsganss, a well-funded Republican Christian activist who led the conservative takeover of several metroplex school boards. He won by 14 points in a January special election for a State Senate seat covering a region that Mr. Trump won by 17 points in 2024. A ‘Gradualist’ Theory Which party prevails in Texas is a complicated riddle. Historically a low-turnout state — it ranked second to last in the 2024 election, ahead of only Arkansas — Texas held a primary in March that saw nearly one in four voters showing up to the polls, a modern record for midterm participation, with Democrats slightly outpacing Republicans. A few factors could conspire to thwart a blue wave in Texas. As of 2020, straight-ticket voting is no longer possible in the state, which could impact the mostly Democratic urban counties where that practice has frequently been used by voters in past elections. Texas is one of only eight states that lack universal online registration, while voting by mail is also highly restricted. In January, Mr. Abbott turned over the state’s list of approximately 18.7 million registered voters to the Trump administration, and 1.2 million of them have subsequently been put on the “suspense list” because their addresses have not been verified. The recent shuttering of nearly one-third of Tarrant County’s polling sites by its Republican-controlled county commission is particularly worrisome for Democrats. “The reason we’ve lost these statewide races in the past is because we’ve never gotten enough out of Tarrant County to overcome the margins in rural Texas,” Ms. Davis said of the turnout. “If we don’t get it to 53 or 54 percent this November, it’s game over. James and Gina can’t win.” But the state’s Republicans have reasons of their own to be fretful. Partly because of the recruitment efforts of the Texas Majority PAC and Blueprint Texas, a down-ballot candidate support organization co-founded by Ms. Davis earlier this year, the Democrats are fielding a full slate in all 150 state races for the first time in a half-century. Though many of these aspirants face long odds, their presence on the ballot could energize the Democrats in predominantly conservative regions who have not bothered to turn out in the past. “If we win on Nov. 3, most of those names running down-ballot in really tough areas like East Texas and the Hill Country and the Panhandle will be responsible,” Mr. O’Rourke said. Mr. Henson added that while he remained skeptical about Democratic enthusiasm being sufficient to carry the day for Mr. Talarico, he also doubted that a last-minute avalanche of negative ads would prove decisive for Mr. Paxton. “At a certain point, there’s diminishing impact once you get past an absurd level of spending,” he said. Rather than project a winner in November, Mr. Henson said he felt more comfortable embracing a “gradualist” theory, one in which Texas does not become blue overnight, but instead competitive. “Even if Talarico loses by a Beto-like margin,” he said, “the next cycle is a presidential election, where Trump likely won’t be popular and Democratic turnout will be higher. So there are reasons for Texas Democrats to be optimistic.”' You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:

In less
than two weeks, voters decide who controls the Senate. That means they’re
choosing the future of our courts.

Here’s the truth: The courts decide nearly everything. Whether your rights
survive. Whether you can get the care you need. Whether your vote counts.

Sooner or later, every one of those fights lands in a courtroom. More and
more often, the judge hearing it was picked by Trump.

And he’s filling the federal bench with loyalists. Partisan hacks who know
exactly who they owe their robes to. They get lifetime seats and will be
ruling for decades after Trump leaves office.

But this part matters the most: Trump can’t seat a single judge without
the Senate.

So November comes down to one choice. Either the next Senate majority
keeps handing Trump a bench that answers to him, or Democrats take the
majority and use their power to block his most dangerous picks.

Every seat that flips is one more senator who can vote no on Trump’s
cronies.

Demand Justice PAC makes sure voters see that choice. We drag Trump’s
nominees into the light, expose their extremist records, and make every
senator own their vote.

Trump and his allies have spent years building courts that serve them. We
have to make sure everyone knows this election determines if that keeps
happening.

name: Amy Acton
subject: Hear me when I say: this is who Vivek Ramaswamy is.
body:
|
#
| | | | | Hi, Peter – Roy Cooper here. My friend Amy Acton is running for Governor in Ohio, and she needs our support. If you can, [**_I hope you'll split a donation between our grassroots campaigns._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/20101?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1638&amount=5&t=7&akid=4861%2E124072%2EIUn6Vs)

If you'd no longer like to receive these partner emails, [**_you can opt out here._**](https://act.roycooper.com/signup/unsub-tandems/?t=8&akid=4861%2E124072%2EIUn6Vs)
---|---
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/20101?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1638&amount=5&t=9&akid=4861%2E124072%2EIUn6Vs)
Peter, I can’t make this up. Vivek Ramaswamy has unleashed attack ads against me that have gone too far.
He’s stooped so low that even Republicans are calling him out. He’s showing Ohio exactly who he is: **a man willing to go to despicable lows to win.**
**But the fact of the matter is the polls still show this is anyone’s race.** Experts are calling our election _the most competitive governor’s race in the country, so even a few hundred votes could change things._
[**_I’m urgently asking you to split a contribution between my campaign and Roy Cooper to help me fight back and win this election, not just for me, but for the people of Ohio. Even $3 can make a difference._**
| | | [DONATE $3](https://act.roycooper.com/go/20141?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1638&t=11&akid=4861%2E124072%2EIUn6Vs)
---
| | [OTHER AMOUNT](https://act.roycooper.com/go/20101?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1638&t=12&akid=4861%2E124072%2EIUn6Vs)
---
Look, our state deserves a leader with integrity and compassion, Peter.
But Vivek Ramaswamy has proven to us time and time again that he has neither of those things.
I refuse to sit by and let a self-serving billionaire ruthlessly hurl disgusting, personal attacks at me and others to get what he wants.
**We need to send a clear message: this kind of hate and vitriol has no place in Ohio.**
But I’ll be frank – we’re still being outspent by a large margin, and if we allow him to dominate the airwaves for these final 10 days, we’ll be at a real disadvantage on Election Day.
[**_Peter, I know I’ve asked a lot of you these last few days. But this is one of the most important elections in our state’s history. Whatever you can give today will go directly towards supporting our grassroots campaign to defeat Vivek Ramaswamy and Roy Cooper’s campaign for U.S. Senate. >>_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/20101?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1638&amount=5&t=13&akid=4861%2E124072%2EIUn6Vs)
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Amy Acton and Cooper Victory Fund will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/20102?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1638&amount=5&t=14&akid=4861%2E124072%2EIUn6Vs)
---
| | [DONATE $25](https://act.roycooper.com/go/20102?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1638&amount=25&t=15&akid=4861%2E124072%2EIUn6Vs)
---
| | [DONATE $50](https://act.roycooper.com/go/20102?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1638&amount=50&t=16&akid=4861%2E124072%2EIUn6Vs)
---
| | [OTHER AMOUNT](https://act.roycooper.com/go/20101?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1638&t=17&akid=4861%2E124072%2EIUn6Vs)
---
Thank you for sticking by me,

Amy
| |
* * *
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1638&t=1&akid=4861%2E124072%2EIUn6Vs) Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

**_[Donate today to help win this seat and flip the Senate blue.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1638&source=&t=2&akid=4861%2E124072%2EIUn6Vs)_** | | [DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1638&source=&t=3&akid=4861%2E124072%2EIUn6Vs)

No images? [Click here](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-e-fhtehy-hhlljjcji-u/) **For Immediate Release:** October 23, 2026**Contact:** Kylie Glatfelter, Communications Director, [kglatfelter@indiana.gop](mailto:kglatfelter@indiana.gop)**Nieshalla and Elliott Put Fiscal Responsibility and Hoosier Taxpayers First****Indianapolis, Ind. **- The Indiana Republican Party is highlighting a new ad spotlighting State Comptroller Elise Nieshalla and State Treasurer Daniel Elliott's commitment to keeping taxes low, making life more affordable, and protecting Hoosier taxpayers.The ad highlights Governor Mike Braun's gas tax holiday, which has provided more than $1 billion in savings to Hoosiers, and emphasizes the importance of responsible financial management. Both Nieshalla and Elliott serve on the State Board of Finance, which has worked to reimburse local governments for revenue lost during the gas tax suspension.**WATCH THE NEW AD BELOW:** [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhtehy-hhlljjcji-r/) [Watch the new ad highlighting fiscal responsibility, tax relief, and efforts to keep Indiana affordable.](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhtehy-hhlljjcji-y/) "Hoosiers deserve transparency, accountability, and responsible stewardship of every taxpayer dollar," said State Comptroller Elise Nieshalla. "From strengthening financial transparency to ensuring our local communities receive the funding they depend on, my focus remains on giving Hoosiers a clear picture of how their tax dollars are managed and holding government accountable to the people it serves.""Fiscal responsibility means making smart decisions today that protect taxpayer dollars and preserve Indiana's long-term financial stability," said State Treasurer Daniel Elliott. "As Treasurer, my responsibility is to safeguard public funds, manage state investments wisely, and ensure taxpayer dollars are working for Hoosiers. My focus remains on transparency, accountability, and responsible financial management."Nieshalla oversees Indiana's accounting and financial reporting, including the Indiana Transparency Portal, while Elliott serves as the state's chief investment officer, managing state investments and safeguarding public funds."Elise and Daniel have established records of fiscal leadership in their respective offices," said Indiana Republican Party Chairwoman Lana Keesling. "From excellence in state financial reporting to strong investment returns, their work has produced measurable results for Indiana. Those accomplishments give Hoosiers a record they can count on as they head to the polls on November 3."**Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, 2026.** Indiana's future belongs to the Hoosiers who show up. Make your plan, bring a friend, and make your voice heard at the ballot box.### [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhtehy-hhlljjcji-j/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhtehy-hhlljjcji-t/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhtehy-hhlljjcji-i/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhtehy-hhlljjcji-d/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhtehy-hhlljjcji-h/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fhtehy-hhlljjcji-k/) ** PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE. ****NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE OR CANDIDATE'S COMMITTEE. ****WWW.INDIANA.GOP.** | Indiana Republican State Committee 101 W. "From strengthening financial transparency to ensuring our local communities receive the funding they depend on, my focus remains on giving Hoosiers a clear picture of how their tax dollars are managed and holding government accountable to the people it serves.""Fiscal responsibility means making smart decisions today that protect taxpayer dollars and preserve Indiana's long-term financial stability," said State Treasurer Daniel Elliott. "As Treasurer, my responsibility is to safeguard public funds, manage state investments wisely, and ensure taxpayer dollars are working for Hoosiers. My focus remains on transparency, accountability, and responsible financial management."Nieshalla oversees Indiana's accounting and financial reporting, including the Indiana Transparency Portal, while Elliott serves as the state's chief investment officer, managing state investments and safeguarding public funds."Elise and Daniel have established records of fiscal leadership in their respective offices," said Indiana Republican Party Chairwoman Lana Keesling. "From excellence in state financial reporting to strong investment returns, their work has produced measurable results for Indiana. Those accomplishments give Hoosiers a record they can count on as they head to the polls on November 3."Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Indiana's future belongs to the Hoosiers who show up. Make your plan, bring a friend, and make your voice heard at the ballot box.### PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE.
