name: Rick Bennett
subject: $400 million in political ads. Imagine the alternative.
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Bennett for Governor · P
body:
Reject outside dark money and put those resources toward helping Maine families instead.

| | |
---
---
---
---
Peter,

On Thursday I held my final town hall where I rejected outside dark money and called for putting those resources toward helping Maine families instead.

**In today’s corrupt system, too many wealthy special interests use staggering amounts of money to influence our elections.** These dark money forces pull the strings behind the scenes as the full scope of their influence remains hidden from public view.

Here in Maine, we can expect to see over $400 million spent – in the U.S. Senate race alone. That is enough to provide free meals to school age kids for the next 10 years.

More money is going to negative attack ads in the Maine Senate race than is allocated to winter heating oil assistance for the entire state.

These groups that are dumping millions and millions into Maine’s elections do not care that Maine families are struggling with higher housing costs, higher energy bills, and higher health care costs. They see Maine people’s pain as nothing more than political opportunity.

So Thursday in Freeport, alongside many of you, **I called on not just Hannah Pingree and Bobby Charles – but also Troy Jackson and Susan Collins – to reject the hundreds of millions of dollars in out-of-state dark money flooding this election, and to ask those organizations spending that money to direct it towards helping our friends and neighbors in need.**

Mainers do not need another toxic TV ad or mendacious mailer telling them how bad the other guy is. We don’t accept a scorched earth politics engendering fear and hatred. Mainers need affordable heating oil, housing that is within reach, and healthcare that is accessible.

**I ask you to put your money towards organizations and community groups that will truly help our neighbors in the coming months.**

But, we still need your help in these final few days:
1. [Watch this clip and share it with three people you know who are tired of the same two parties running the same playbook.](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=0ZEw3rKCYdU6QDR4jANpCzJgPR1oXz7mjSdU-TTQM5mRE2riSovjnJJrr-Ndr714VARBWAQV-bkxq8JBwrpMycUtg6GH60CRjan247V_fUZXM9e6p2nwLF_O7kD4ya-eLWYZvXDM9C9mgbFyoXE3RSnX1H8oFIJIEHMIjRhr3phUto2EMlNQY2HgmYDzWZrj_puGP8LWgQKCsyuiSIoVGx3n8JA0HBNwPOTWlnLS6LRW9GtC8XgmaBMtr_525Ej9&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=10_23_money_in_politics&n=1)
2. Talk to your neighbors about this campaign. A personal conversation moves more votes than any ad.
3. Make your plan to vote, and help someone else make theirs.

Thank you,

Rick
---

Our volunteers are personally texting the voters in their networks. These aren’t spam texts. Our volunteers reach out 1:1 and have real conversations to share resources and voter reminders.
This is a real convo between one of our volunteers and a voter in our network before early voting started this last Monday:
Nothing beats personal, human to human connection.
And we know this is the work that works because in 2024, the young voters we met in this way turned out at over 79%, compared to a statewide average for young people of 39%.

## Melania Brokers Truce in Ukraine City
Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a [localized ceasefire](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1yqzAQRp8GOjHS8iNRqLgNnW-bklnBYm8swLMIE799hsRvkPbszM53zselvyBHXq7_cSafprVf6NgipUTSzxRxYQyy3km2JPtA9DUFxh40NMpoBVWPQ-In9SYf_UQEVObkjW3BldY6k998HRoH0DRgWhe0MzpQsGOoy7GuXKNtzv58ZzRURkNbtgUEbY1zE07aYWkpqzSNnFYpPlde0o2m-FqfJMWwznn0t5QeW1b-y6DLoDuOo1jCcGqc95OsEscMuv0uyAtl0Mm-bYzqDRRehUgNhBtNLKQGTi_1a02jeldQSfb5oWRYsNE1GJuLHx8Hx8hbY7NKX2fk-DMp_S3k08N3AAAA__952olS) in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, Ukraine, brokered by first lady Melania Trump, the White House said Friday. The truce is set to [begin Oct. 29](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOnDAQhJ_GdEb22gdc4SIN3Z82JVpgfWzOYGSbI7x9RJQ3-LuRRhrN9_36Gr6QA2-vn7iSKz4OG505UCmUhpUCboxjim9KuaRjIvrjR8YBFDRSKwl2wKnwhwZdzc4TAZmKnG6f0Jm27XS1OECcHg3aRwPKGrIPmkijNaozZrSdrtjdc1qB1Qqe5lnDqFrddR696tC0JKyimUtM9e_IW1nIhyt-KNVTXKvgllL2LMwPAb2A_jzPehrzjXH3Avo7Cug9p1xkwPmS_8FkSce6y0LrHhOmS06EmTwnkunImVEe74S8kYyB8vK-BPRVcvN-cgicm1ZY9VqRw78j5Xv6Pg7-BgAA___2wIcV) and is meant to let humanitarian aid in and move civilians out through a designated safe passageway. Melania Trump said the remaining residents are mostly elderly and need medicine, food, and clean water. The White House said the first lady and a representative worked directly with both governments on the terms. Oleshky, once a city of about 24,000 on the Dnipro River, [fell on the first day](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGu3CAQQE-DO1Yw8I23oEjjbtOmtDAelsliYwFeZ28fOcoNfvekkebNm1-P6eEo0fb86Va0LeRpw7MmbA3LtGJyG7m55BeW2srhEf-EmdwEAnouBQc9Od_ojZPsFhsQAVWHVpo7DMqYQXbR6kX2Snt_X9RX_-WVEXroe0BtZqmEwY7stU4K0FLAXd1vMAsjhyG4IAanDDItcKGWy-13pq1FDOmT31huPq9dsrG1vTL1g8HIYDzP8_aqrl1DBuOVw2Dcc6JG_sJLxmCU4mLFYPyfyVs51p1HTHvlIZcnco-uYqCCfEGXOG28HLWS23j2_tgJF54T1vj68BaRn5Ea8piPiry6zyXril32k1Ki2humxXN1lP7d3b737beFvwEAAP__mXqU0A) of the 2022 invasion. Moscow has not commented publicly. Ukraine's top negotiator said the humanitarian operation would begin once the truce takes hold.
## Ex-FBI Agents Charged in Hunter Biden Case
Two former senior FBI officials surrendered on arrest warrants Friday after being [charged with lying to Congress](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu3CAURL8Gd1hwcYy3oEjjbtOmtABf7JtgsIBdZ_8-8vuF14000mjO-f1cnpYipe2XPdC0kJeEV43YGpblwGgTWVfyXyy1lZdH_Bcc2QUEjFwKDsNifaM3LrJbTUAEVB0aqR8wKa0n2e3GyRGFHQH9Dz0obcFrqVwQ0zop1KA7MvecFDBIAQ_16MEJLacp2CAmqzSyQeBKLZf-T6bUdgzxk99Yep-PLpq9tbMy9ZPBzGC-rqv3rt4Yd89gviODOTjiOQTyZGPlfrdlw5XHD6WNt8x9TlvBWvn-Sg0Ld7Ri4tGeLZ8M5q6Y9bwoRqqjZoPYDkvx60D7nra3gf8BAAD__6r-g6g) about the bureau's Hunter Biden investigations. Nikki Cole Floris, 46, and Bradley Benavides, 56, who ran the now-dissolved Foreign Influence Task Force, each face [one count of making false statements](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0E2SnSAUQOHV6AwLgVYcMMjEWWeaocXPRW8H4RVcNW_3qWQLvYFTp75fn9unxYR5_2lPMBTLluFpCYigbickm9G6Wn5DbVQvD_AnOrSb4GJiI2dCbdYT3rCNfTARQIDswYzzIrScZz32h1F6cV5O4HlYrJRR6VF-TMBnFz6UCrpH8y83cqFGLha5DMLxedQ62si1lTN0ikNAKnX4KpjpgJje5YY6-HL2yRxEr9bJH51YO7E-zzN8XY3Qw7CXuxPr1WxhwXdifdVOrPQUFks9obLokJUY0aNNjfnD1h0CS2_MO_Ml7xVaY9aVi9hxZYLKHAbIDPMNjXC3hCW3vprwejAlbNPcKb6fFtP_N_qe6G3E3wAAAP__eDOOcw). Both told the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 that the task force played no role in the Hunter Biden cases. Benavides testified that he first learned the FBI had the laptop by [reading a Wikipedia article](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2u4yAQBeCnwR0RjJ3YLii2cZdtt7T4GezZxWABTjZvf8V9hduNNJpPc86f5_rUFChuv_WBqvq0RnyXgLViXg8MOpI2Of3DXGq-LOJ_b0ivIODBpeAwrNpWeuEqO6c8ImDfoZLjDFM_jpPsduUGPRl3x97cZz0KLb1_WASYhblbM2BHqnFSwCAFzP18AyNGOU1eezHpfkQ2CHRUU779TRTrjj580gvzzaajC2qv9Sys_8VgYbDEz5lKbSsGS4MZLFK0uWewXIW3gAwWb4gn78mSDoW_98RtM9Hx6-T7FStmbshh5EGfNZ3c7jpv6LhPmYcPxY3XdhO3jKWBXVbufFMIVB4jG8R2aArfL9afFftS8BUAAP__GRGOSw) in 2023. Prosecutors say he discussed the laptop routinely with FBI colleagues before the 2020 election. Attorneys for Floris called the case "nonsense" and noted it was filed [10 days before](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO2zAQRU9DdTTIoS3KBYs06jYIkCKlMCKH0mQpcUHO2tnbB84VUn_g47336215Qy58bt_xoCC5Lic9eyERastBBU_GtdV3al3aZyT6k1fGBQyM2hoN1wWj8IMWO6SQiYDcQMH6O0zO-8kOewBKK8EtTYjZ3Ufjc3IZrR3HiLfk7cDhdWcNXK2Bu7tfYDXeTlPGbCZ0ntTVUGKp7fK78ik75fJVH9QusR5DCbvIR1fum4JZwYxrfCm8NgXzj1pYOHYF85Mb_ZTavhTMoPPKuubMkbF0HXdsGyV94Dufm85YOukuKHTQKV3vn6dQ09b5mzU354cW0seTS-E-enU124Fc_uHI_0V8BPgbAAD__y0mh_Q) the Nov. 3 midterm elections. The judge refused a prosecution request to delay the preliminary hearing for more than two weeks and set the hearing for Tuesday.
## Ranking: Ballparks from Oldest to Newest
The World Series opened last night in Milwaukee with the Brewers beating the Tampa Bay Rays 3-2 in a 25-year-old ballpark that sits right in the middle of a new [ranking of all 30](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OozAQAJ8GOiN7TfgpXFxDl2uvRGtYJ74sGNkbuHv7T_le4etHM9L8uc93jBz3x2_cyElI805XYRKhPG_EuEf0Ob0oF8nvhehf8BFn0NApoxW0My4ST5pNvbpABGRrcqYfYbB9P5j66W52QLt0o0eDAdphNWPb4tgZb_F281BH99EZDa3RMNqxAa97MwwBgx7Q9lS1mtYoKTd_U9zlSYH_p5Nys6StZvcUOUplf1UwVTBd19WcsbyRFzyiIMciH7CCKeP-olVt7JVH5gPzq6iQ06YSr1RESVI7XVSkgqnObj2uyBxL11etfmwY-bsoP_t0OvgKAAD__14GfqA) major league parks by age. Fenway Park, which opened in 1912, and Wrigley Field, from 1914, are the only two ballparks left that predate 1960. MLB dates every park to its [first regular-season game](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAUheGnwRsWXGywB4Yu3tK1o4XDJaEBE8Ft3L595b5C5yN90vk_LuvFxRT327vLaCmUdcejJSTCumZMbo9uq-WBtVH9uiJ-hy26FQRoLgWHYXVXii9cZedtQARUHVppZpiUMZPs7hbVGLQfYdOgvVbjbAYDM-jJ-WHUDrpoT04KGKSAWc09bMLIaQouiMkpg2wQ6COV2n-WuNMdQ_opL6z9teQu2TvRszH1xmBhsBzH0ee0nRuD5XzDYMlp409XH42HWjIvyWMjToXveGCjrlr_PGJKsWnDBnHLLqY_nf7X5GXhNwAA___UgXYi). Only five parks are at least 40 years old, and 19 of the 30 opened between 1990 and 2009. clean_body: Friends, Early voting starts today. You do not have to wait for Election Day. | Friends, Early voting starts today. You do not have to wait for Election Day. You can walk in this weekend, cast your ballot, and be done. | Early voting runs every day through Sunday, November 1. Election Day is Tuesday, November 3. Each county sets its own hours and locations. Your early voting site may be different from the place you usually vote on Election Day, so check before you go. Here is why your vote matters in this race. Tom DiNapoli has sat in the Comptroller’s chair for nearly 20 years. He oversees a pension fund worth more than $300 billion and is supposed to be the one watching how Albany spends your money. Five late budgets. Spending that keeps climbing. Waste found after the money is already gone. New Yorkers deserve a Comptroller who protects their retirement, their tax dollars, and their future. They deserve an independent watchdog. I came to this country from Cuba at seven years old. My father was a political prisoner. I know what it means to live in a place where your vote does not count. Here, it counts. Every single one. Make your plan today: 1. Pick your day. 2. Look up your site. 3. Bring someone with you. | One more thing. Forward this email to 3 friends, family members, or neighbors who need the reminder. Races like this are won by the people who show up early. Thank you, Joseph Hernandez Republican for NYS Comptroller P.S. We are spending this final stretch reaching voters across the state. A $10 donation becomes $70 through New York’s matching program. | | Hernandez for New York, 697 3rd Avenue, #106, New York, NY 10017

## I-30 Shuts Down in Downtown Dallas
All lanes of I-30 through downtown Dallas [close at 10 p.m.](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAQQL8Gd7OCMWvsgiKNu0ub0hrDeE0Ow8qQ5fbvI0f3B6mf9KT3fn0sHxRiSI-fdLCtX1teErcSuVY-l9DLsv-pPrd0UEohPTY6QnyvC0ocQElAvZCr4cWLps7bVfpJdWyVmXDsJ6NNt9sBx35Y7wbd3Q-rZ0mD8ZthHtV4V6Ppgr10SqJWSiL2N2mUdGYk7Yxf2UuhJftQ83mrO1f-orLFd37xeXP56KLda30W0f8QOAucW2u3tDq_tQsLnK8igXPMjqLA2VOMVODI51UE39RReucEzzP_ZlehhRjBxVwYKEYI0EuIlLhASHANqbkl-FbVPRRozJ-cPOx8coG2U4Wa4TPlJnDWctIGe4Fzd1r_vOyhDEZo-TgoxH8d9X__vyz-DQAA__8Gq5yA) tonight and stay shut until 5 a.m. on Monday. The closure covers both directions between I-35E and the I-45/U.S. 75 interchange, with traffic detoured onto Woodall Rodgers Freeway (Spur 366). TxDOT is urging drivers to avoid the area if they can. The shutdown is part of the $888 million I-30 Canyon Project, which broke ground in March and runs through 2031. The Texas A&M Transportation Institute ranks the Canyon as the state's 11th most congested corridor. Some crossings will stay closed long after this weekend: [Botham Jean/Lamar Boulevard](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFurDAQRb_GdEb2YGEoXLyGbl-bEg32sFgxZgUTzP59RKR8Qboz0uhenfvxGB8YU8zP_7iS42vexkzlSMRM-xgbdSxfHLaSV8w55ueMa0zvaQQFrdRKghnRczxpNFgFN6nQ64qctj10TW-NrRYXJttpbLzCvgOktp1bMgZa8tM8gQ5VdHecVmC0VgBNraxW3nZovA0TBSWMohB522teiOnCY07v7aS99ttaJbcwvw7R_BMwCBhKKfW8XeYWuR8EDDcKGH5lZJSNkjfxfQVMCQ9J14s8U5CF6JNyqHYXXiWmFI_WCqOeK8b008h_Xep08B0AAP__aAl_-w) through late 2027 and Cesar Chavez Boulevard through late 2028. Austin drivers also will be hit with detours this weekend as [downtown streets close](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGS4yAQRL8GZbhghCU5ILhE2V56oWosBmtqEWyJsfD-_ZX3PuHi7nrVr_98LB_IifPjN-7k5RXLkqnVRCJ0LNybuj0llJZ3zJnzI-LO6fu-gIFBW6PBLbgKn7Q47IK_m3CzHXk73mDqb6Mbu83HdYgu2okGF-g6gJkQpmBdD-56NaHv2L9x1oCz1gD0FzNas44TunUMdwpGOUOBpRwX2UjohTWm73LScVnL3iW_iXxV1f9SMCuYW2uXzxfmd6hgfvsomFNZMSmY8VmFs4K5ykEkek2lPg-qmrN-i0ppWf8radm46kb0STnoWA4drT75RJ1QnxxQR6rC5w-3O3z4apwS12FUzjx25PSzT_7319PD3wAAAP__3zqPiw) for today's Viva La Vida Day of the Dead festival and the Formula 1 U.S. Grand Prix, which wraps up Sunday at Circuit of the Americas.
## Texas SNAP Enrollment Hits 17-Year Low
Texas SNAP enrollment hit a [17-year low](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unTAMx58mbDlKTIDLkKEL2-3aERliwGpIEHEPl7evuFKfoJuln_z_-vU5fiJHTutP3MnL15LHRFeJJELnyLUp2x8J-Uo7psRpXXDneE8jGGi1NRrciLPwm0aHVfCTCb2tyNuuh4-671xXbb6F2jQNUht6a6CZWqqN62FuXNOa0C4V-0fOGnDWGoD6ZTpr5u4D3dyFiYJRzlBgyedLNhL6wrLEO7_pfM15r6LfRI6i6h8KBgXDdV2v3wXlgQqGp4-C4ftNwfBYKRisee76H9Al4aEPPIVnPlA4Jx3OfBQtWaO2nb4JTx3zpbFo2UgvFIoWXjehpCnyyhNHllvBUJ0-HBfHyKXtlDPrjhy_o8r_Tvz28DcAAP__YuKQGA) of 2.8 million in September after falling 20.8% in a year, the steepest drop in two decades, with children making up more than half the losses. The drop follows last year's federal budget law, which extended work requirements to more parents and adults up to 64. It also [ties state costs](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOtSAQhZ9GuzGAKFpQ_I3d_dstzSCjkkUwinp9-4032SfYaorJ9-Wc8_XqX-i8C9N_XEin9xj7QNfuKSXaeleyfT6SjVdYMAQXphEX52_TCyZq4AyE7HFI7qReYm61YbblOWmuWtGUrZIqn3VrVCUJleCmrm3Z4KCqsmmqsaqMrKs6d_rRcSYk50yIsmCKs0E1KAdlDVmWSUbWpbgVaaZEb9xHf8eTtmKIS-71nNK6Z-W_THSZ6K7rKr7fGJ5nJrqnTya6D_Z7YcEbZjwJUoQVb1CshcV572KAMW6wB1zhCJY2iIHAuAkM4ZHceHgwznvYDk-PL9-0Xa8H3WuVSTYt6PwnV_rrnqcWPwEAAP__uCiLrQ) to error rates, and Texas could owe up to $2 billion in 2028-29 if its nearly 9% rate doesn't drop below 6%. Just 64% of applications were processed within 30 days, down from 91% last year and below the [federal 95% benchmark](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDuupDAQAE9jMpBpvJgJHGxC9jbdEPXYDbTkD8I98Ob2q9krvLikUqn-fi1fyJHz9gcTOfley5LprpFE6Fx40HV_SSh3Tpgz523FxPH9XEDD2Pa6BbOgF75oMdgE99Th0TfkevuAaXhYY5vdBU0rwaCHYKxBo0dv6Jcfx9GCnsyEDbuPrtdg-l4DDJ22vfZ2QuNteFLQymgKLOXsZCehb6xrfJeLzs6X1ES3ixxVDb8VzArm-767NdfuVQN2W7kUzDXjoWDGkDgrmDkdZ7k4b20VFGqFE0XOVGt7olBtqXqMKFxye5zFf8D24oDZU3O6cNwcI9fRKqO3hBz_d8hP_10O_gUAAP__K7CH5A). HHSC said new mandates "require a thorough review of each case."

A note from Senator Ashley Moody |
---
Peter,
I'm going to be honest with you, because I don't know any other way to say this.
My heart breaks for France right now. City halls burning to the ground. More than 600 police officers injured in a single day. Rioters tearing the French flag off the monument to their own Republic – and raising a Palestinian flag in its place, while others march under the hammer and sickle.
Communists and radical Islamists, side by side in the streets. **That 's not a coincidence. That's an alliance.** And it has eyes on more than Europe.
This radical movement is working to infiltrate our own country – and it's counting on patriots like you not realizing it until it's too late.
It is the honor of my life to serve as Florida's U.S. Senator. My state is full of people who already know how this story ends. Families who fled Castro with nothing but the clothes on their backs. Venezuelans who watched their country get looted by socialists in a single generation. Nicaraguans who escaped Ortega. They came here because America was the one place it couldn't happen.
Here, that movement has a fellow traveler on the ballot, and her name is **Angie Nixon.**
She runs a bookstore called "Cafe Resistance." On its wall hang portraits of convicted cop killers – including Assata Shakur, who murdered a New Jersey state trooper and fled to Castro's Cuba. When she was confronted about it, she said she stands by "everything in this bookstore."
She closes her speeches with a line from the Communist Manifesto – "We have nothing to lose but our chains" – and she took that chant to a CAIR gala. She was one of just 7 votes against teaching students the history of communism. She signed the pledge to abolish ICE. She voted against tougher penalties for people who assault police officers.
And she just raised $7 million to take Florida's U.S. Senate seat – more than we raised in the same three months. And Bernie Sanders just pointed his $23 million war chest at this race and came to Florida himself to campaign for her and turn out the vote.
This is a special election – the biggest Senate race in the country this year – and some new polls say it's within the margin of error. If she wins, she becomes **the first dues-paying member of the Democratic Socialists of America in the U.S. Senate.**

My husband is a police officer. I spent my career as a prosecutor, a judge and an attorney general. I've stood with the families of officers who were attacked. I've stood in rooms full of people who escaped communism and wept when justice finally came. I made them a promise: _not here. Not in America._
**I can 't keep that promise alone.**

## _Dispatch from Paris:_
As soon as we touched down in Paris yesterday we hit the streets to see how locals are preparing for the October 24th scheduled demonstrations.
The air was filled with tension, and cigarette smoke as Parisians prepared for the worse.
## [Watch here:](https://substack.com/redirect/865a4736-80a4-435e-bf75-e6c05e02ed3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/865a4736-80a4-435e-bf75-e6c05e02ed3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Click To Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/865a4736-80a4-435e-bf75-e6c05e02ed3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
President Macron issued citywide curfews and even deployed military units for crowd control after last weekend's protest devolved into violent and destructive riots.
Shop owners near Place de la Republique, the site of last week's riots, were boarding up their businesses frantically. Smashed windows and torn-down entry ways marked the entire strip.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/0a18be07-4b1b-4220-96a2-f5580201268b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I asked as many people as I could if they thought Saturday's protest were going to be as violent or worse than the prior week's. The consensus: _" Oui."_
"I'm afraid the government is not ready," one man told me.
Several said that the blame lays with Macron's government refusing to act on student grievances related to crowded class sizes, underfunded schools, and teacher pensions.
I asked how destruction of property and historic monuments will achieve their goals. Many expressed disagreement with the violence, but agreed that it is an effective way to force the government's hand to take action.
"Why are we seeing communist and Palestinian flags at these protests?" I asked. "What does that have to do with student demands?"
"We want to stop support of Israel and that genocide," one man who apparently partakes in the protests told me, a response I heard from several people I spoke to yesterday.
"I think it's a lot of causes that unites them to make a bigger voice," he explained.
French conservative presidential candidate Marine Le Pen's chances of winning the April election surged recently correlating with the riots and Macron's weak response to unrest.
Le Pen now has **[a 50% chance of victory on Kalshi's odds](https://substack.com/redirect/81c94e8c-6eac-46c9-b78e-95da06ce70a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as more french people identify with her stricter immigration agenda and conservative fiscal policy proposals.

* * *
_**(Piece continues):**_
I also asked them to respond to President Trump's hypothesis, that open borders and France's lax immigration policy are largely to blame for the unrest and the obvious presence of migrant and 2nd/3rd gen immigrant rioters.
"They (the french government) wanted violence! That's what they were waiting for! So they can say 'see, I was right, those people are animals, those people are not supposed to be here!" one girl told me.
"Has mass migration been good for France?" I asked.
"Of course! It is a racist country. They have so much fear, they don't know where to put their fear. Society will grow (by mixing)," she explained.
That was the answer I heard most frequently from these parisians, that open borders has nothing to do with the riots and migration from the third world has been a great success for their country.
I am not convinced by this answer personally, based on the video reporting I've seen from previous riots of what appear to be islamist activist partaking in violence and destruction. But today, I will have the opportunity to see for myself who is involved as a mass gathering is planned for 2 pm Paris time at the former site of the Bastille where a monument to the french revolution stands today.
The government is taking this protest much more seriously than prior weeks, deploying riot police **[and even military units](https://substack.com/redirect/acbaf9a0-a134-45bd-82f6-209241648700?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to keep the crowd under control.
"The deployment next Saturday will be massive," Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, explaining that the immediate priority was to restore order after what happened on October 17.
Our team will be publishing footage**[live to X](https://substack.com/redirect/b9b085d3-7d75-4551-a763-c2b7e54a4836?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and other social platforms including on YouTube on **[our PolitiBrawl Streetcast channel](https://substack.com/redirect/dd8c795a-09b2-428b-b661-33a9a46c2f38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** throughout the evening.

We asked Parisians who is REALLY behind the riots... | | | Oct 24 | | | | | | | | | | | | Dispatch from Paris: As soon as we touched down in Paris yesterday we hit the streets to see how locals are preparing for the October 24th scheduled demonstrations. The air was filled with tension, and cigarette smoke as Parisians prepared for the worse. President Macron issued citywide curfews and even deployed military units for crowd control after last weekend's protest devolved into violent and destructive riots. Shop owners near Place de la Republique, the site of last week's riots, were boarding up their businesses frantically. Smashed windows and torn-down entry ways marked the entire strip. I asked as many people as I could if they thought Saturday's protest were going to be as violent or worse than the prior week's. The consensus: " Oui." "I'm afraid the government is not ready," one man told me. Several said that the blame lays with Macron's government refusing to act on student grievances related to crowded class sizes, underfunded schools, and teacher pensions. I asked how destruction of property and historic monuments will achieve their goals. Many expressed disagreement with the violence, but agreed that it is an effective way to force the government's hand to take action. "Why are we seeing communist and Palestinian flags at these protests?" I asked. "What does that have to do with student demands?" "We want to stop support of Israel and that genocide," one man who apparently partakes in the protests told me, a response I heard from several people I spoke to yesterday. "I think it's a lot of causes that unites them to make a bigger voice," he explained. French conservative presidential candidate Marine Le Pen's chances of winning the April election surged recently correlating with the riots and Macron's weak response to unrest. Le Pen now has as more french people identify with her stricter immigration agenda and conservative fiscal policy proposals. | | ---|---|--- Get $25 in credit to trade on Kalshi after you sign up using our code "brawl" or by Kalshi supports independent media like PolitiBrawl! (Piece continues): I also asked them to respond to President Trump's hypothesis, that open borders and France's lax immigration policy are largely to blame for the unrest and the obvious presence of migrant and 2nd/3rd gen immigrant rioters. "They (the french government) wanted violence! That's what they were waiting for! So they can say 'see, I was right, those people are animals, those people are not supposed to be here!" one girl told me. "Has mass migration been good for France?" I asked. "Of course! It is a racist country. They have so much fear, they don't know where to put their fear. Society will grow (by mixing)," she explained. That was the answer I heard most frequently from these parisians, that open borders has nothing to do with the riots and migration from the third world has been a great success for their country. I am not convinced by this answer personally, based on the video reporting I've seen from previous riots of what appear to be islamist activist partaking in violence and destruction. But today, I will have the opportunity to see for myself who is involved as a mass gathering is planned for 2 pm Paris time at the former site of the Bastille where a monument to the french revolution stands today. The government is taking this protest much more seriously than prior weeks, deploying riot police to keep the crowd under control. "The deployment next Saturday will be massive," Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, explaining that the immediate priority was to restore order after what happened on October 17. Our team will be publishing footage and other social platforms including on YouTube on throughout the evening. name: Swing Left
subject: Trump is traveling to red states to rescue GOP Senate candidates. Here’s how we fight back.

body:
With just 10 days left until Election Day, there are signs everywhere of the shifting momentum.
#
Hi there,
**With just 10 days left until Election Day, there are signs everywhere of the shifting momentum** —not least of which is the fact that Donald Trump is traveling to red states like Texas and Alaska in an attempt to rescue Republican Senate candidates whose polls show they are in serious trouble.
In response to efforts by Trump and Republican super PACs to boost their candidates in this final stretch, **we’ve updated the Immediate Impact Fund. It now includes the 20 House and Senate candidates where donations will make the biggest difference** in ensuring candidates that will impact the national balance of power can stay competitive right when many voters are tuning in and starting to cast their ballots.
Today, we want to take a deeper dive into the Senate candidates in the fund. [**Read below for more details, and then make a donation to the Immediate Impact Fund today.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=immediate-impact-2026.DM5m6O&utm_source=ak&amp%3Butm_medium=em&amp%3Butm_campaign=iif-2026&amp%3Butm_content=20261024-2&amp%3Brefcode=ak_em_iif-2026_20261024-2&t=1&akid=3271%2E1562180%2EmCvAe6)
* * *
**Mary Peltola, Alaska**
Former Democratic Representative Mary Peltola is in a strong position to defeat incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in this red state, where local issues like high energy costs and salmon bycatch are dominating the campaign narrative.
Republicans are desperate to claw out a win, however: Just this month, Donald Trump and JD Vance both visited the state. Plus, Republican super PAC Americans for Prosperity just put another $3.4 million into the race, increasing the Republican advantage in outside spending. Peltola needs the support of the Swing Left community to make sure GOP spending doesn’t tip the scales against her in this final stretch.
* * *
**Josh Turek, Iowa**
Iowans are tired of Republicans’ failed policies. At the same time, simultaneous open races for U.S. Senate and Governor for the first time since 1968 are providing an opportunity for Democrats, who haven't held a U.S. Senate seat in the Hawkeye State in over a decade. But Democratic nominee, state representative, and Paralympian Josh Turek has proven he can win in a Trump district.
While Democrats held a primary, Republicans quickly coalesced around incumbent Representative Ashley Hinson as their preferred candidate, giving her time to stockpile campaign funds. Polls show an incredibly close race, but since October 1st, Republican outside groups have dropped a staggering $39 million plus into this race, attacking Turek and supporting Hinson. Hinson also ended June with almost three times as much money in the bank as Turek, so it’s essential he has the financial support he needs to talk to voters in every corner of the state.
* * *
**Adam Hamilton, Kansas**
One of our target Reach races, the Kansas Senate race has become increasingly competitive over the last few weeks, with nonpartisan analyst _Cook Political Report_ recently moving it to a “Toss-Up.” The last three public polls show Democratic candidate Adam Hamilton, the pastor of the largest church in the state, pulling ahead of incumbent Republican Senator Roger Marshall. Marshall has come under fire for a number of issues, but most seriously, his former medical practice sued more than 700 patients over unpaid bills, and 81 people were arrested after missing court appearances connected to the cases.
Republicans are so concerned about this race that they pulled their spending out of the North Carolina Senate race and shifted it to deep-red Kansas, which hasn’t elected a Democratic Senator since 1932. Hamilton needs our support to stay competitive against the GOP’s last-minute spending spree.
* * *
**Abdul El-Sayed, Michigan**
After a competitive primary, Abdul El-Sayed clinched the Democratic nomination and now faces former Republican Representative Mike Rogers. Recent polls have Abdul El-Sayed with a narrow lead over Mike Rogers, and with a race expected to be one of the most competitive in the country, it could determine control of the Senate.
El-Sayed got a boost last week when Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez transferred $1 million to support his campaign in the final stretch, but Republicans are also spending heavily to help Rogers. With such a narrow polling lead, support from the Swing Left community can ensure El-Sayed remains ahead.
* * *
**Troy Jackson, Maine**
After Graham Platner dropped out of the U.S. Senate race, Maine Democrats chose former state senate leader Troy Jackson as their new nominee. Since then, Jackson has had a very short window to raise money and build a campaign capable of defeating longtime Senator Susan Collins—and Republicans wasted no time launching false attacks, trying to define him before more voters could get to know him. Despite this, Jackson has been competitive in polls with Collins, but he’ll need continued financial support to compete with Collins on the air and on the ground.
_ProPublica_ recently reported allegations that donations to a Collins-supported super PAC were connected to efforts to secure federal contracts. Jackson needs immediate support to ensure voters understand that after 30 years in the Senate, Susan Collins is working for her donors, not Mainers.
* * *
**Scott Colom, Mississippi**
Scott Colom, the elected district attorney for Mississippi’s 16th Judicial District, is putting Mississippi on the map with his strong campaign to represent the state in the Senate. His opponent, incumbent Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith, recently came under fire for implying, in response to a question about rising beef prices, that people could “pick another protein.” Plus, in another sign that Republicans know they are losing support in red states like Mississippi, there have been reports that they will try to redistrict the state after the midterm elections.
Mississippi is one of our Reach races, and Colom needs support to keep building name recognition and get his message out to voters in these final critical weeks.
* * *
**Chris Pappas, New Hampshire**
Former Republican Senator John Sununu is running to regain his seat and is considered a top recruit for Republicans. While Democratic Representative Chris Pappas has led narrowly in most polling, recent polls have shown the race tightening, and Republicans are heavily outspending Democrats.
The _Cook Political Report_ just moved this race back to “Lean Democrat” from “Toss Up,” and Pappas needs immediate support to maintain his narrow lead.
* * *
**Sherrod Brown, Ohio**
Former Senator Sherrod Brown, a champion for workers' rights, is running to flip JD Vance’s Senate seat against the appointed Republican incumbent, Jon Husted, in a high-stakes special election. Despite Ohio’s recent red shift, polling shows Brown holding a single-digit advantage.
Unfortunately, Politico just reported that _“A cryptocurrency super PAC funded primarily by Trump-aligned billionaires Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss is pouring almost $3 million into the Ohio Senate race to help block Sherrod Brown from returning to Washington.”_ We can’t let these crypto billionaires buy Ohio’s Senate seat—Sherrod Brown needs immediate support to counter their dark money.
* * *
Across the country, campaigns are finalizing their last TV buys of the cycle while deciding how much to put into digital ads to mobilize voters in these final 10 days. With Republicans outspending Democrats by more than $320 million in key tossup races, Democrats risk being drowned out just as voters head to the polls.
[**Will you make a donation of $25 or any amount to the Immediate Impact Fund today to support the Senate candidates above, in addition to the House candidates in the races where control of Congress will be decided?**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=immediate-impact-2026.DM5m6O&amount=25&amp%3Butm_source=ak&amp%3Butm_medium=em&amp%3Butm_campaign=iif-2026&amp%3Butm_content=20261024-2&amp%3Brefcode=ak_em_iif-2026_20261024-2&t=3&akid=3271%2E1562180%2EmCvAe6)
**[Donate $25 »](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=immediate-impact-2026.DM5m6O&amount=25&utm_source=ak&utm_medium=em&utm_campaign=iif-2026&utm_content=20261024-2&refcode=ak_em_iif-2026_20261024-2&t=23&akid=3271%2E1562180%2EmCvAe6)**
Thank you, as always, for everything you do,
The Swing Left Political Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20261024-2&t=24&refcode2=3271_1562180_mCvAe6&akid=3271%2E1562180%2EmCvAe6)

subject: Elon Musk vs. ActBlue

body:
#
**$455 million.**
That is how much money Elon Musk has personally spent this year to help Republicans hold the House and the Senate. That number is not up to the second, so as you read this the total is likely higher.
Let me put that number in perspective for you.
**$275 million.**
That is how much money was donated to Democratic federal campaigns and committees across all of ActBlue during the month of September alone. That money was raised from more than 6 million individual donations giving an average of around $40 apiece.
Think about that.
In this country, we have conditioned ourselves to accept as normal that one man can have a greater financial impact than 6 million donations from regular folks who are acting to elect people they believe will prioritize their needs over the needs of people who already have it all.
And what does Elon Musk do it for?
A. As the richest man in the world, he does it for his own tax cuts and,
B. His billions of dollars for his own federal contracts.
And that is just one man. Nine of the top ten donors this cycle are Republicans according to the _Washington Post_. These numbers are as of more than a week ago.
* Elizabeth & Richard Uihlein: $138 million
* Jeff & Janine Yass: $110 million
* Ben Horowitz & Marc Andreessen: $92 million
* Miriam Adelson: $68 million
* Cameron & Tyler Winklevoss: $55 million
* Paul Singer: $54 million
* Greg & Anna Brockman: $50 million
* Christine & Stephen Schwarzman: $36 million
Do you think they give that money as an act of charity? I think we all know how this works. These mega-donors are giving that much money because they are expecting a return. It's an investment.
And the outcomes we get are not a surprise.
That is oligarchy.
From the start, I have funded my campaigns differently because I believe you cannot accept the same money that is used to oppress the working people of this country.
There are a lot of folks in races tougher than mine who say it's naive to swear off that corporate money.
I say it's what we need.
I say it's what you deserve.
You deserve a government that answers to you, not the people writing the checks.
You deserve a government that takes on corporate greed rather than takes their money.
Our average donation is $16.
I am very proud of that fact.
Because in the history of this country, great change has almost always come from the bottom-up. It happens when lots and lots of people are willing to stand up and say ENOUGH and to fight for what we believe in.
We may not raise as much as Elon Musk gives, but we do raise quite a bit ... and most importantly the way we do it tells me we are on the right track. That we are building the foundations of a movement with the ability to take on the greed of the billionaire class in this country.
And the truth is, the single greatest source of donations we receive comes in response to emails like this one. Which means if we are going to continue to fund our work, our organizers, our rallies, our donations to progressive candidates... it means from time-to-time I have to ask:
[ Can you please make a contribution to my campaign today? Our average donation is around $16. Some give more. Some give less. All that matters is that lots and lots of people are chipping-in and the rest will take care of itself. ](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-26-q4.h3BeQC&refcode=em20261024-12473-P_FND_EXP_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12473%2E2526796%2EyamAY0)

Thank you for your continued support.
In solidarity,
Alexandria

name: Douglas Carswell
subject: Why we built the Mississippi Wire
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/whyismssoawesome-12855253?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
Who is reporting on your county board of supervisors? Your school board? Your city council? A generation ago, the answer was obvious. The local paper sent a reporter. He sat through the meeting, took notes, and you read about it over breakfast the next morning. Today, across much of Mississippi, the answer is no one. Local newspapers did not decline because people stopped caring about what happens in their town. They declined because Big Tech took the advertising that paid for the reporting. The classifieds went online. The display ads went to Google and Facebook. And the reporters who used to cover the courthouse were let go. That matters more than it might seem. Self-government depends on people knowing what their government is doing. Thomas Jefferson put it bluntly — offered a choice between government without newspapers or newspapers without government, he said he would not hesitate to prefer the latter. When no one is in the room, officials answer to no one. Decisions about your taxes, your schools, and your roads get made without anyone outside the building ever hearing about them. So we decided to do something about it. We built the Mississippi Wire. I have recorded a short video explaining why. In it, I set out how the local newspaper model broke down, what has been lost as a result — and how the Wire uses new technology to do the kind of reporting newspapers used to do, region by region, from the Delta to the Coast.

You can watch it [here](https://us.list-manage.com/bzUecpPdpwE?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3).
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/ft_x3czXFfo?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)
---
| The Wire is not about opinion. It is about telling Mississippians what their officials said and did - plainly, and in time for it to matter. Big Tech hollowed out local news. It turns out new technology can help bring it back. Please take a few minutes to watch the video, and then take a look at mississippiwire.news for yourself. Have a wonderful weekend!

|
Peter,
Attorney General Todd Blanche was asked whether the Justice Department would try to stop states from certifying the midterm results. He refused to rule it out.
And now we know why.
The Department of Justice just sued the state of Alaska to block the certification of election results if Democrat Mary Peltola defeats MAGA Senator Dan Sullivan.
---
---
| | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001h3aAbIvL-UzUwKRNxUhRSSjM_J3CDoyAw5XY7LLegOaH9qgr6ErLCxbY0sZNilXYfCfavRO3KtSs0nZboIPmjLTHxAzm0iUHEbYMFXRRBNgDjMDir_CmoH_Y3PN_mPTzMVktD6RAg0JfKaSeExw6Y6cuv5l_iT1Z8zY3nVC1AUWvbUWwxK68ck62zjGcAuHLUH2dzqd2nh5jNfo1SwwXl9yzynTDmITySC0vv5Gf5fm9687SiwI98Q==&c=C0kqx1mRZ_14Ce92FGCCddNMpMGA3EZ3agD8uOlDe6bSfXtbQbseHA==&ch=V9NNO8wrIqO4ywvritCej4oZtdrvfIVLpO_cIslHBtjzK1zlKXBopA==)
---
They're trying to rig the results before a single vote is cast.
Their excuse? A second candidate on the ballot also happens to be named Dan Sullivan. He is a retired teacher who chose to run. On the ballot, he is listed as "Daniel J. Sullivan Jr." with no party label, while the senator is listed as the Republican incumbent.
MAGA already tried to kick him off the ballot and the Alaska Supreme Court said no. So now Trump's DOJ is asking a federal court to do what the state's highest court would not: hand them a way to throw out the result if their candidate loses.
We need our courts to hold the line. In 2020 they did just that, throwing out over 60 Trump lawsuits that attempted to overturn the election results. We need them again this year.
This is why Defend Our Courts exists.
First, we are building a firewall of state supreme courts that protect free and fair elections. Alaska just showed why that matters. Its Supreme Court already stood up to Trump and MAGA once.
Second, we are turning out Democrats in key Senate and House races, so that when they try to steal a seat in court, the margin is too big to steal.
The coup has officially begun. With only 10 days until the election, we need the support of Dems everywhere to defend and build pro-democracy majorities on key state courts. He refused to rule it out. And now we know why. The Department of Justice just sued the state of Alaska to block the certification of election results if Democrat Mary Peltola defeats MAGA Senator Dan Sullivan. | | == They're trying to rig the results before a single vote is cast. Their excuse? A second candidate on the ballot also happens to be named Dan Sullivan. He is a retired teacher who chose to run. On the ballot, he is listed as "Daniel J. Sullivan Jr." with no party label, while the senator is listed as the Republican incumbent. MAGA already tried to kick him off the ballot and the Alaska Supreme Court said no. So now Trump's DOJ is asking a federal court to do what the state's highest court would not: hand them a way to throw out the result if their candidate loses. We need our courts to hold the line. In 2020 they did just that, throwing out over 60 Trump lawsuits that attempted to overturn the election results. We need them again this year. This is why Defend Our Courts exists. First, we are building a firewall of state supreme courts that protect free and fair elections. Alaska just showed why that matters. Its Supreme Court already stood up to Trump and MAGA once. Second, we are turning out Democrats in key Senate and House races, so that when they try to steal a seat in court, the margin is too big to steal. The coup has officially begun. name: Team Molly
subject: Weekend reading: St. Albans Messenger Endorses Molly
body:
Dear Peter, Hot off the press! Yesterday, the _St. Albans Messenger_ endorsed Molly for Lieutenant Governor, and we wanted to share the good news and give you a little weekend reading. In his endorsement, Editor Emeritus Emerson Lynn made the case for why Molly is the right choice for Vermont: “In the lieutenant governor’s race between Republican John Rogers and Democrat Molly Gray, the candidate who best meets Vermont’s needs is Ms. Gray...For two basic reasons: first, she’s a strong communicator, and second, we need someone in the office who is willing and able to take on the Trump administration’s persistent attack on the country’s civil rights... Ms. Gray has the talent we need. She has the experience that will make her efficient in the job. She is the communicator who can bring us together to solve our challenges. And, most importantly, she has the integrity necessary to weave together Vermonters who need to know they are being told the truth. **[If you’ve been waiting to chip in to Chris Pappas, I’m asking you to do it right now. Not next week. Right now.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261024_3.JzVy42&refcode=em20261024-3&t=1&akid=9746%2E582294%2EHXFOSD)**

Here’s what we’re up against. Republicans are spending **$66 million** to take this seat. Those Sununus have been running New Hampshire politics like a family business for more than forty years. John Sununu’s daddy was governor. His brother was governor. Now John wants his old Senate seat back, even though Granite Staters showed him the door in 2008.
National Republicans know exactly what this race means. New Hampshire is a Democratic-held seat. If they flip it, there’s no path to a Democratic Senate majority. If Democrats hold it, we may just flip the Senate.
Chris Pappas has won the toughest district in New Hampshire **_four damn times_**. He knows how to close. But closing costs money: ads in the final stretch, mail hitting doors, organizers knocking from Nashua to the North Country. Every dollar that comes in this week will be spent before Election Day. A dollar that shows up after November 3rd doesn’t win us a damn thing.
**[So here’s my ask: $10, $25, $50, whatever you can spare, to support Chris Pappas today.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261024_3.JzVy42&refcode=em20261024-3&t=3&akid=9746%2E582294%2EHXFOSD)**

I’ve sat in too many rooms on election night watching a race we should’ve won slip away by a few thousand votes. Every time, somebody says, “If we’d just had a little more at the end.” We can’t let that happen in New Hampshire.
**[In a race this close, the dollar you give today might be the difference, and I’m not exaggerating. Chip in $25 now, and help Chris finish this race strong.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261024_3.JzVy42&amount=25&refcode=em20261024-3&t=5&akid=9746%2E582294%2EHXFOSD)**

Let’s win this damn thing and flip control of the Senate.
– James Carville

Hi friend, Governor Gretchen Whitmer here. I was just in New Mexico with my friend Deb Haaland, and I’m all in to help her become the state’s next Governor. With just 10 days until Election Day, friend, there’s too much at stake for New Mexico’s future to sit this one out. [**Will you chip in $5 right now to help Deb reach voters across New Mexico in these final days?**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17387?refcode=jtk1664-fr-nd&amount=5&t=2&akid=13433%2E400544%2EB114Mg)
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17387?refcode=jtk1664-fr-nd&t=3&akid=13433%2E400544%2EB114Mg)
---
Across the country, we’re seeing what happens when Washington puts politics ahead of people. Families are struggling with rising costs, healthcare is under attack, and our fundamental freedoms are on the line.

_New Mexicans are feeling the consequences of Donald Trump’s policies, and they need a Governor who will fight for them.
_
That’s why Governors matter now more than ever. We need leaders who will put working families first and fight every day to make life better for the people they serve. I know that’s exactly the kind of Governor Deb will be.

When I was in New Mexico, I saw firsthand Deb’s determination to build a better future for her state.
As Governor of Michigan, I've worked to fix more than 26,000 lane-miles of roads, provide free breakfast and lunch to 1.4 million public school students, and put money back in the pockets of working families. That's what it means to deliver real results for the people you serve. **I know what it takes to turn promises into progress, and Deb is ready to bring that same results-driven leadership to New Mexico, making life more affordable and ensuring every family has the opportunity to thrive.**

But friend, we can’t take this race for granted. A new poll shows Deb’s Republican opponent within striking distance, and he wants to bring Trump’s harmful agenda to New Mexico. Republicans are investing heavily in this race, and we can’t afford to fall behind.

With just 10 days left, every bit of grassroots support matters. Let’s make sure Deb has the resources to get her message out, reach voters in every corner of New Mexico, and finish this campaign strong. [**Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can to help Deb reach voters and win this race?**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17387?refcode=jtk1664-fr-nd&t=4&akid=13433%2E400544%2EB114Mg)
Thanks for being in this fight with us.

Gretchen Whitmer

body:
It was a tough choice
Peter, it’s Eugene Vindman. I just made the toughest decision I’ve had to this election cycle and need to share it with you.
Over the weekend, my opponent launched another attack ad against me. It’s an ad made entirely with AI, and it implies I am hurting working Virginians' paychecks. On top of that, he’s linking to a website he’s created, devoted entirely to slandering me.
My team and I came together to determine our response strategy, and our best option was to urgently expand our advertising and voter outreach efforts to compete with his ads, set the record straight, and get undecided voters on our side before Election Day.
That meant expanding our TV ad buys and putting more organizers on the ground. Those are pretty steep expenses, Peter. But with nearly two weeks until Election Day, I gave my team the green light.
Here’s the problem you need to know though:
It wasn’t an easy decision. Let me quickly explain:
**We don’t have the money in the budget to approve this expense. But I took the risk anyway because it’s what we need to do to win — and because I bet on this team, knowing you will help us fill the budget gap.**
That’s how much faith I have in this team and our fight to hold this seat, flip the House blue, and stop Donald Trump.
Peter, I know for a fact that we have two advantages in this race: our commitment to defending our democracy — and you.
We can't afford to leave voters unreached in a race this close. I'm counting on grassroots supporters like you to help fill the gap we've created by investing more in reaching voters before Election Day.
I hope you'll step up and join us in this fight.
So, on the heels of my difficult budget decision, I’m asking:
[**Can you make a $3 contribution to my campaign today? Your donation will help us fund the voter outreach we need to win this race.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-oct26?refcode=em261024-av&refcode2=1167_3892029_7LPPDG&akid=1167%2E3892029%2E7LPPDG)

body:
We have 10 days left. Let me explain what's at stake. |
---

Fellow Patriot -

Here's a breakdown of our race ... _by the numbers_.

**$9 million:**
This is how much Annie Andrews raised last quarter.
I got into this race long after she was already raising millions of dollars from liberals all over the country. She has the support of Hollywood stars like Star Wars' Mark Hamill and Roseanne's John Goodman.

**3 months:**

A note from Senator Ashley Moody |
---
Peter,
I'm going to be honest with you, because I don't know any other way to say this.
My heart breaks for France right now. City halls burning to the ground. More than 600 police officers injured in a single day. Rioters tearing the French flag off the monument to their own Republic – and raising a Palestinian flag in its place, while others march under the hammer and sickle.
Communists and radical Islamists, side by side in the streets. **That 's not a coincidence. That's an alliance.** And it has eyes on more than Europe.
This radical movement is working to infiltrate our own country – and it's counting on patriots like you not realizing it until it's too late.
It is the honor of my life to serve as Florida's U.S. Senator. My state is full of people who already know how this story ends. Families who fled Castro with nothing but the clothes on their backs. Venezuelans who watched their country get looted by socialists in a single generation. Nicaraguans who escaped Ortega. They came here because America was the one place it couldn't happen.
Here, that movement has a fellow traveler on the ballot, and her name is **Angie Nixon.**
She runs a bookstore called "Cafe Resistance." On its wall hang portraits of convicted cop killers – including Assata Shakur, who murdered a New Jersey state trooper and fled to Castro's Cuba. When she was confronted about it, she said she stands by "everything in this bookstore."
She closes her speeches with a line from the Communist Manifesto – "We have nothing to lose but our chains" – and she took that chant to a CAIR gala. She was one of just 7 votes against teaching students the history of communism. She signed the pledge to abolish ICE. She voted against tougher penalties for people who assault police officers.
And she just raised $7 million to take Florida's U.S. Senate seat – more than we raised in the same three months. And Bernie Sanders just pointed his $23 million war chest at this race and came to Florida himself to campaign for her and turn out the vote.
This is a special election – the biggest Senate race in the country this year – and some new polls say it's within the margin of error. If she wins, she becomes **the first dues-paying member of the Democratic Socialists of America in the U.S. Senate.**

The order arrived in Finnish, but it might as well have been written in lumber. Finland's Licensing and Supervision Authority -- the LVV -- has demanded that Tuike Finland Oy, the company representing Google, "immediately suspend, and no later than 23 October 2026, all preparatory measures that would significantly alter the environment" at two planned data center sites: Muhos, near Oulu, and the village of Otanmaki, outside Kajaani. The deadline was yesterday. The order had to exist at all because most of those "preparatory measures" were already history: by local estimates reported by the Guardian, roughly 250,000 trees felled at Muhos -- some 330 hectares, 815 acres -- plus an estimated 150,000 more at Otanmaki, the topsoil scraped off behind them. All of it before the environmental impact assessment Finnish law requires was finished. The regulator is now investigating whether the felling was even lawful, with enforcement and fines on the table. If it wasn't, the wood is worse than gone. Timber felled illegally cannot be sold to the mills.
Google's Finland country manager, Antti Jarvinen, apologized last week -- while maintaining the company believed it was acting legally. The company has also promised to plant trees across 130 hectares of Muhos as part of its biodiversity work. Which is very Google: under order to stop altering the environment, its biodiversity program advertises planting the environment back. Hanna Halmeenpaa, chair of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, gave the local review: "They bought the vast land area and they just started to cut it, just like that. It's pure arrogance and it's amazing."
Finland is one entry in a genre. In Mason County, West Virginia, advocates with the Global Justice Ecology Project report that a grove of some 200 blight-surviving American chestnuts -- planted in the 1970s from wild survivors, a living "genetics library" for a species the blight all but erased -- stands at the former Clements State Tree Nursery, land once owned by Mark Twain's grandparents, in the path of Nscale's Monarch Compute Campus, where Anthropic is a prospective tenant. The advocates say clearing could begin November 1. The caveats are heavy: the companies have confirmed none of it, no permit has surfaced publicly, and the developer reportedly says the grove isn't inside its footprint. But notice what the dispute is about. Not whether the trees matter -- where they sit.
Outside Fort Wayne, Indiana, the method is fully legal, which is the point. Hatchworks, the developer of Google's $2 billion, twelve-building campus, has already won state permits to fill wetlands -- including 2.13 acres of forested wetlands approved this September -- with roughly 8.5 acres of wetlands filled or slated for fill by local count across the early phases. The compensatory mitigation will happen somewhere else in Allen County, because the law does not require the wetland to survive where the wetland lives. Every permit is in order. The swamp is still gone.
And in Vineland, New Jersey, the method got caught running hot. DataOne's data center operated 62 large natural-gas generators with no state permits -- undiscovered until the newsroom Floodlight flew a thermal drone along the fence line and counted 45 of them running. In September, the state Department of Environmental Protection issued its largest-ever fine against a data center: $1.07 million -- this while the same industry gets blamed for New Jersey's rising electricity bills. Data One disputes the findings and says it will apply for the permits. After. A record fine, against an industry spending tens of billions a quarter, is not a deterrent. It is a utility bill.
Put the four sites side by side and the verdict on "big tech is anti-conservation" comes into focus -- with a correction. Nobody in these stories hates trees. Google pledges carbon-free energy by 2030; Anthropic named itself for humanity's long lineage and built its brand on safety. What the sites share is not malice but ordering: assess after clearing, permit after trenching, fine after running, negotiate the footprint while the dozers warm up. Conservation, in practice, is process -- an assessment, a hearing, a comment window -- and process costs time, and time is the one thing the AI buildout will not spend, because the company that computes first wins. So the environment keeps getting filed in the wrong column: pre-construction gets the chain saw, post-construction gets the questions. A wetland can be offset in another county. A fine can be amortized. A genetics library cannot be mitigated at all. When the penalty is priced below the cost of waiting, compliance stops being a constraint and becomes a line item -- and an industry can be earnestly green in its marketing while being reliably anti-conservation in its sequencing. The trees never get a vote. They get a date.
Finland at least produced an order with a date on it, a national petition demanding data-center regulation, and an argument over why Finnish renewables should power someone else's machines. West Virginia has a date too, and it is the trees that have to meet it. The assessment was supposed to reach Muhos before the chain saws. It didn't. Somebody's project schedule decided that.

You've heard Democrats talk about a "blue wave" this year. But what's really powering their Senate campaigns is a GREEN WAVE of cash. And it's crashing over the Senate map right now. Look at the latest FEC reports, covering July through September: ▶ **TEXAS** : James Talarico (D) raised $60.2 million. Ken Paxton (R) raised $10.2 million.
▶ **KANSAS** : Adam Hamilton (D) raised $9.4 million. Roger Marshall (R) raised $800,000.
▶ **GEORGIA** : Jon Ossoff (D) raised $33.1 million. Mike Collins (R) raised $2.8 million.
▶ **FLORIDA** : Angie Nixon (D) raised $7.2 million. Ashley Moody (R) raised $2.1 million.
---
[](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=29df15edccdc40c39cd94af4bffc903c&_e=dEeO1YQXlnHKL6hhL25Irln_0d3vsGEw56uaTdUDnpJYyUr0vK8GI26WlG_gaopISmi91u3yy9UVgeVSDboP6kq1_dwFz6bbu591AJLMeY6sbneoQdj9dINln5tkraXvg4xqU9-m9RHQupskZLBC7oX-HJLz-raNblaXOW8Q079AtNojO2jF3DnmDJ2SIqy-kX7Bknz1EIx094cDjVOXvPZQBOLWDB-zGIvyZXDdm1RzbOAEDXklf_2B5uZ56Yvk0RYDTvHcXn_bCy1d21MO8eM8wFvyW2NZQrdU-XCG__sefsJy1Iu0Mc5MoqOQHapWW6jHIgUQgdUID0s7E4Hn2r5xkFcHx18-dH9mzJ4OJtb8XuMsd8-57VltbEc90ugRM_rLGl0z6C-PHzSpWpQ9Ug%3D%3D)
---
You may have seen headlines bragging about record Republican super PAC money. The GOP's top Senate super PAC just raised a record $272.9 million in a single quarter. Here's what those headlines leave out: **a super PAC dollar doesn't go nearly as far as a candidate dollar.** Federal law requires TV and radio stations to sell ad time to candidates at their LOWEST UNIT RATE in the final 60 days before a general election. That's the same rate the station gives its best commercial customer. Super PACs don't get that rate. They pay whatever the station charges. During a football game in Austin in September, a Republican super PAC was charged $450,000 to air a single ad. Talarico's campaign paid $50,000 for a spot in the same game, in the same market. **That's NINE TIMES the price.**
---
[](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=29df15edccdc40c39cd94af4bffc903c&_e=dEeO1YQXlnHKL6hhL25Irln_0d3vsGEw56uaTdUDnpJYyUr0vK8GI26WlG_gaopISmi91u3yy9UVgeVSDboP6kq1_dwFz6bbu591AJLMeY5Sj-lO2xE7505GjUF7Gbf3cYppETwp9e8XVEHq3tQfUXYMgEE_qYG87aJtpTa3vmH6zbnH9NASBoMFOeMtZ6gVLLmoRPqz07HBm5ArKE4R7-P0Yag9G6sJS0ub4gNOQEjHZviPbNv9Peb_KX1RuG1JU2G-tTy2VP4Hs4quGdZzRZ_-CWbRiGWQ8MwfHa6-AF2gwaLQvn_zka62aB95S6116SjuBOyQ1mTOKYwJ8Z94X0LZIZVKzpA8-OUrn-BYXHNffVYvV-6Rez4vAjsJ39ISyrXkRouWfHMWsB8zYAj2pw%3D%3D)
---
**So when Democrats send money straight to their candidates, every dollar buys MORE airtime than a super PAC dollar.** And that's exactly what they're doing. For years, the Left has built a national small-dollar machine. Liberal donors don't just give to candidates at home. They give to candidates in states they've never visited. Talarico has raised more than $122 million from individual donors this cycle, and more than $65 million of it came from small donors giving $200 or less. If James Talarico wins in Texas, it will be because of that mountain of small-dollar contributions. **[We need to use the same national model to fight back: direct contributions to our candidates.](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=29df15edccdc40c39cd94af4bffc903c&_e=dEeO1YQXlnHKL6hhL25Irln_0d3vsGEw56uaTdUDnpJYyUr0vK8GI26WlG_gaopISmi91u3yy9UVgeVSDboP6kq1_dwFz6bbu591AJLMeY4ZLOQtaDM8_XWJ40fRiuv7oyVgW0iy6Ixfg8UQBIp6DtBonn7auylAlv99qDc8JXbtDIqdN53YTOOmJWmd7mAtUNSEdwrxbMswR1ccGGiienQ-iXtM3J7WNnR91SNxpJ7dL3lo67LMiEIJgVR3PKcUlwSwnuP24T9sxJ1wwhSs7FEfdllPgOz5vWKh4VoT71IubO14WINXOHqtoy55LVXMnR0I5y7PhmUg8lH7y3CG2oOYC4Y3vNCKU0v08HwI5s0XwrYl7lYx63HZHtYN9kZN-oHWs0fgBPmMRSzLa8cCaw%3D%3D)** Once your money moves away from the candidate's own campaign, it buys less. That's why the Senate Conservatives Fund makes it easy to give directly. You can support multiple candidates with a single, secure transaction. But what's really powering their Senate campaigns is a GREEN WAVE of cash. And it's crashing over the Senate map right now. Here's what those headlines leave out: a super PAC dollar doesn't go nearly as far as a candidate dollar. Federal law requires TV and radio stations to sell ad time to candidates at their LOWEST UNIT RATE in the final 60 days before a general election. That's the same rate the station gives its best commercial customer. Super PACs don't get that rate. They pay whatever the station charges. During a football game in Austin in September, a Republican super PAC was charged $450,000 to air a single ad. Talarico's campaign paid $50,000 for a spot in the same game, in the same market. A Jewish lesson: leave it better than you found it

---
| | There’s a Jewish concept I learned from my mother and grandmother long before I could spell it. It’s called _tikkun olam_. It means “repair the world.” It’s the obligation to leave things in better shape than you found them. My mom and grandma spent their lives working through the National Council of Jewish Women and Hadassah, and my mom eventually served as president of NCJW. They believed that if something was broken, it was your job to help fix it. In 2018, I became the first Jewish woman elected to Congress from Virginia, and I brought that lesson with me to the Capitol.
I passed a bill securing **$455 million to restore the Chesapeake Bay**. And when the Capitol came under attack on January 6th, I joined the January 6th Committee to uncover the truth, knowing it could cost me my seat.
It did. I’d make the same call again.
Right now, Washington is deeply broken. I’ve never turned my back on my country when it needed me, and I’m not about to start now.
The other side knows what’s at stake, too. **MAGA groups have now spent $8 million to keep Jen Kiggans in this seat.**
Eight million dollars can tear a lot of things down. It’ll take all of us working in unison to protect what we’ve built here in VA-02.

We need all the help we can get to fight back against the $450,000 Mike Johnson just dropped into this race, so if you’re able, I’d be incredibly grateful if [**_you could chip in a few bucks to my campaign and Jeremy Moss._**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142087488/655767175/1027041474?refcode=BLU_EM_MOSS_2026-10-24_01&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc5OTIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTRkNWFjYjctYjNjZi1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=W42ahxcAtSBBfXZBHVtpDrbeJ03dW9Jr1bEDP7kSuUc=)

**But, if you have a minute, I also wanted to explain not just why I’m asking for your support, but why I decided to run for Congress in the first place.**
I was born and raised here in Michigan, a public school kid from modest roots. Now I’m proud to be raising my own kids here in Kalamazoo, and I’ve spent most of my life serving this community, first as a City Commissioner, then as a state representative, and now as a state senator.
To me, leadership is all about solving problems and making life better for the people you serve, which is what I’ve worked to do every day as a public servant — whether it was cracking down on slumlords, leading disaster relief with the Red Cross, or delivering tax relief to Michigan’s seniors and working families.
**Fundamentally, being a good leader means living your values. And the reason I’m running for Congress is that Washington has never seemed more out of touch with the values I’ve spent my life fighting for than it does right now.**
Right before I entered this race, my opponent Bill Huizenga _was one of two deciding votes_ to throw 450,000 Michigan residents off their health coverage. And boy did that cement my decision to run against him!
**But even since that absolutely disgraceful and disqualifying vote, Huizenga has continued attacking the Michigan families he’s supposed to be serving.**
He voted to gut the Affordable Care Act — raising health care premiums all across our country this year. You’re probably paying higher bills because of this, and so is almost everyone you know.
He’s stood against accountability for ICE and refused to exercise any of Congress’s oversight powers to hold Donald Trump or his administration to account.
And when some of Huizenga’s constituents visited his office to try to peacefully share their concerns? Huizenga’s office _wouldn’t even unlock the door._
**Put simply, the people of Michigan deserve better leadership. And I’m determined to give it to them. So yes, I’m running to end Bill Huizenga’s political career. Proudly.**
But to get this done — and not just “come close” or score some worthless moral victory — I need your help. Unlike so many other candidates, I’m not some self-funding billionaire and I’m not backed by big special interests — so the success of our campaign depends on supporters like you.
[**_So if you’re with me in this fight, and if you support my decision to take on MAGA mouthpiece Bill Huizenga, can I count on you to pitch in to my campaign and Jeremy Moss and power our fight?_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142087489/655767176/1027041474?refcode=BLU_EM_MOSS_2026-10-24_01&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc5OTIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTRkNWFjYjctYjNjZi1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=W42ahxcAtSBBfXZBHVtpDrbeJ03dW9Jr1bEDP7kSuUc=)

clean_body: I just couldn’t sit on the sidelines | | | | = | | Peter, I’m sure your inbox right now is full from campaigns asking for your support. And yes, to be honest, this is one of them (sorry!). We need all the help we can get to fight back against the $450,000 Mike Johnson just dropped into this race, so if you’re able, I’d be incredibly grateful if = But, if you have a minute, I also wanted to explain not just why I’m asking for your support, but why I decided to run for Congress in the first place. I was born and raised here in Michigan, a public school kid from modest roots. Now I’m proud to be raising my own kids here in Kalamazoo, and I’ve spent most of my life serving this community, first as a City Commissioner, then as a state representative, and now as a state senator. To me, leadership is all about solving problems and making life better for the people you serve, which is what I’ve worked to do every day as a public servant — whether it was cracking down on slumlords, leading disaster relief with the Red Cross, or delivering tax relief to Michigan’s seniors and working families. Fundamentally, being a good leader means living your values. And the reason I’m running for Congress is that Washington has never seemed more out of touch with the values I’ve spent my life fighting for than it does right now. Right before I entered this race, my opponent Bill Huizenga was one of two deciding votes to throw 450,000 Michigan residents off their health coverage. And boy did that cement my decision to run against him! But even since that absolutely disgraceful and disqualifying vote, Huizenga has continued attacking the Michigan families he’s supposed to be serving. He voted to gut the Affordable Care Act — raising health care premiums all across our country this year. You’re probably paying higher bills because of this, and so is almost everyone you know. He’s stood against accountability for ICE and refused to exercise any of Congress’s oversight powers to hold Donald Trump or his administration to account. And when some of Huizenga’s constituents visited his office to try to peacefully share their concerns? Huizenga’s office wouldn’t even unlock the door. Put simply, the people of Michigan deserve better leadership. And I’m determined to give it to them. So yes, I’m running to end Bill Huizenga’s political career. Proudly. But to get this done — and not just “come close” or score some worthless moral victory — I need your help. Unlike so many other candidates, I’m not some self-funding billionaire and I’m not backed by big special interests — so the success of our campaign depends on supporters like you. = | | | | | = | | | = | | | = | | | = | | | | = | | Thank you, State Senator Sean McCann Democratic Candidate for Congress, MI-4 | | | | | | = | | | | | | Paid for by Jeremy Moss for Congress | | Jeremy Moss for Congress 2211 S Telegraph Rd PO Box 7023 Bloomfield Hills, MI 48302 United States | | | | | | | | | | = | | | = | | This message was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. | |

body:
Republicans are pouring money into this race. Here’s how we fight back:

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3064%2E4032634%2EZcMds7)

Let me be blunt: Ohio is one of our best chances to flip the Senate, and we can’t afford to lose it. If Sherrod Brown wins, we’re one seat closer to a Democratic Senate that can hold Trump accountable, fight to lower costs, and put working people ahead of wealthy special interests. Republicans know what’s at stake. Outside groups have already poured hundreds of millions of dollars into this race, and GOP-aligned groups are outspending us. The super PACs backing Jon Husted aren’t going to stop now. In these final days, Ohioans will be bombarded with attack ads designed to tear Sherrod down. But Sherrod is a fighter. He’s spent his career fighting a system rigged for the wealthy and well-connected, and he’s running to make life more affordable for working families. And Jon Husted? One of his biggest Senate moves has been nominating Donald Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize. (I’m not kidding.) Early voting is already underway, and we have just nine days left to get this done. What matters most now is whether we can reach voters, organize on the ground, and turn out every last supporter. That takes resources, and the money we raise right now can help power the phone calls, texts, and volunteers Sherrod needs to win. [**So I’m asking: Will you split a contribution of $28, or whatever you can, between Sherrod’s campaign and this movement to help him win Ohio and take back the Senate?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3879?amount=28&t=8&akid=3064%2E4032634%2EZcMds7)

| | | Thousands of North Carolina ballots are on track to be thrown out over minor technical issues. A federal judge just upheld strict new Republican-backed rules for mail voters.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142090238/655776433/-569431239?refcode=261024-NC&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYWYxYjU0OS1iOGNmLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=MuKZarAK2i0PBwrwIAaKsMgyWdcj1vvHCojnEgiRD3A=)
---
The voters weren't doing anything wrong. They just didn't seal a small inner envelope tucked inside a second envelope. That rule was passed on a party-line vote the morning ballots went out. Now some Democratic counties In North Carolina are seeing rejection rates as high as 7 to 8 percent. **This is the playbook. Make voting by mail confusing, make people afraid of it, and then throw out the ballots of anyone who slips up.** Oregon has voted by mail for decades, and it works. That's exactly why it's a target. The same people pushing these rules are also spreading lies that mail voting isn't safe, hoping Oregonians will doubt the system or just stay home. And that’s why it matters so much to have Secretary’s of State who are willing to defend vote-by-mail. **[That is why I am using my campaign to counter disinformation and make sure voters get their ballots sent in, whether it is in Oregon or in other states. Will you chip in $15 to help me do it?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142090239/655776438/-569431239?refcode=261024-NC&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYWYxYjU0OS1iOGNmLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=MuKZarAK2i0PBwrwIAaKsMgyWdcj1vvHCojnEgiRD3A=)**

clean_body: | | | = | | | Thousands of North Carolina ballots are on track to be thrown out over minor technical issues. A federal judge just upheld strict new Republican-backed rules for mail voters. = The voters weren't doing anything wrong. They just didn't seal a small inner envelope tucked inside a second envelope. That rule was passed on a party-line vote the morning ballots went out. Now some Democratic counties In North Carolina are seeing rejection rates as high as 7 to 8 percent. This is the playbook. Make voting by mail confusing, make people afraid of it, and then throw out the ballots of anyone who slips up. Oregon has voted by mail for decades, and it works. That's exactly why it's a target. The same people pushing these rules are also spreading lies that mail voting isn't safe, hoping Oregonians will doubt the system or just stay home. And that’s why it matters so much to have Secretary’s of State who are willing to defend vote-by-mail. = = North Carolina shows us what happens when the people trying to make voting harder get their way. _I just sat down with my friend Stephen A. Smith on his podcast to talk about why I’m stepping off the sidelines to run for Congress in Arizona’s 1st District._ If you know Stephen A., you know he doesn't pull punches. _**I made one thing crystal clear**_**:** **we can’t keep letting career politicians destroy this country.**
* **We must secure the southern border.**

_Living in Arizona, border security isn't an abstract political debate, it’s an immediate crisis. We need real leadership to lock down the border and stop the flow of fentanyl into our neighborhoods._
* **We must deliver economic relief.**

_Inflation is crushing everyday families. I’m running to cut wasteful federal spending, lower taxes, and bring real relief back to AZ-01._
