Friends,
For the past 94 years, every U.S. Senator from Kansas has come from one party. But in just a few weeks, we have a historic opportunity to change that:
🇺🇲 Cook Political Report, Sabato's Crystal Ball, Nate Silver and Steve Kornacki have all shifted their forecasts in our favor, from "safe Republican" to "toss-up."
🇺🇲 According to Roll Call, my opponent, Roger Marshall, is one of the most vulnerable senators in the nation.
🇺🇲 Multiple recent polls show me with a narrow lead over Marshall.
🇺🇲 Five former Kansas Governors -- both Democrats and Republicans -- have endorsed me. So has current Kansas Governor Laura Kelly, lifelong Republican Arch "Pond" Naramore and thousands of people just like you.
When I think about the incredible momentum of our movement, I get chills, but here's the truth: **All the polls, election forecasts and endorsements in the world can 't win an election. The **_**only**_**thing that can do that is votes.**
That's why I want to ask you, right now: **Do you have a plan to vote?**
My wife LaVon and I have made our plan: We'll be voting early and in-person. If you plan to do the same, great! But if not, you can still request a mail ballot or make a plan to vote on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.
Not sure where your polling place is? You can find that information -- plus verify you're registered to vote, check the status of your ballot and more -- at [IWillVote.com](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1908b826-bdff-45ea-b665-a80a1cac02f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
[I Will Vote](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1908b826-bdff-45ea-b665-a80a1cac02f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
As I write this, we're just 10 days away from what could very well be one of the most important elections of our lifetime. What you do between now and then will play a pivotal role in determining whether hardworking families in Kansas and across the country continue to see gas prices increase, grocery prices skyrocket and affordable healthcare driven out of reach -- or if they'll finally get leaders who will fight back against the corrupt and chaotic policies that are causing so much damage.
**Friends, everything is on the line here.** I don't want to wake up on November 4 with a single regret, and I don't want you to either. I want you, me and everyone reading this to be able to say we put everything on the line when it truly mattered.
So please, if you don't yet have a plan to vote, visit [IWillVote.com](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1908b826-bdff-45ea-b665-a80a1cac02f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) right now and make one. And then, if you're able, [please chip in whatever you can to help us finish this race strong](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/5a346f0e-e1e6-4dd8-a245-0c001ed7136e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). With early voting underway and Election Day coming up fast, every dollar makes a critical difference to how many doors we can knock on, how many ads we can keep on the air, how many calls we can make to Kansans in every corner of the state and so much more.
[Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/5a346f0e-e1e6-4dd8-a245-0c001ed7136e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We're in the home stretch. Let's win this.

Votes do. | | | Oct 24 | | | | | | | | | | | | Friends, For the past 94 years, every U.S. Senator from Kansas has come from one party. But in just a few weeks, we have a historic opportunity to change that: 🇺🇲 Cook Political Report, Sabato's Crystal Ball, Nate Silver and Steve Kornacki have all shifted their forecasts in our favor, from "safe Republican" to "toss-up." 🇺🇲 According to Roll Call, my opponent, Roger Marshall, is one of the most vulnerable senators in the nation. 🇺🇲 Multiple recent polls show me with a narrow lead over Marshall. 🇺🇲 Five former Kansas Governors -- both Democrats and Republicans -- have endorsed me. So has current Kansas Governor Laura Kelly, lifelong Republican Arch "Pond" Naramore and thousands of people just like you. When I think about the incredible momentum of our movement, I get chills, but here's the truth: All the polls, election forecasts and endorsements in the world can 't win an election. The onlything that can do that is votes. That's why I want to ask you, right now: Do you have a plan to vote? My wife LaVon and I have made our plan: We'll be voting early and in-person. If you plan to do the same, great! But if not, you can still request a mail ballot or make a plan to vote on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Not sure where your polling place is? You can find that information -- plus verify you're registered to vote, check the status of your ballot and more -- at . As I write this, we're just 10 days away from what could very well be one of the most important elections of our lifetime. What you do between now and then will play a pivotal role in determining whether hardworking families in Kansas and across the country continue to see gas prices increase, grocery prices skyrocket and affordable healthcare driven out of reach -- or if they'll finally get leaders who will fight back against the corrupt and chaotic policies that are causing so much damage. Friends, everything is on the line here. I don't want to wake up on November 4 with a single regret, and I don't want you to either. I want you, me and everyone reading this to be able to say we put everything on the line when it truly mattered. So please, if you don't yet have a plan to vote, visit right now and make one. And then, if you're able, . With early voting underway and Election Day coming up fast, every dollar makes a critical difference to how many doors we can knock on, how many ads we can keep on the air, how many calls we can make to Kansans in every corner of the state and so much more. We're in the home stretch. Let's win this. Adam Hamilton | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Adam Hamilton for Kansas 548 Market Street PMB 72296, San Francisco, CA 94104 ? ?

Sixth in a series of verification studies. The spine, as always: Who decided?
Earlier this month I compared Paris to Beirut and warned the comparison would be abused. It took a week. Since then, three documents have arrived, each claiming to explain the fire: a Fox News Digital investigation called "Chaos Inc."; a State Department statement promising to dismantle the networks behind it; and a viral fourteen-step essay (sections A through H) walking us from a price chart to a theory of why young people blame the wrong villain. All three sell the same product -- a culprit, located before the question. Below, the audit.
**The claim, itemized**
Asra Nomani -- formerly of the Wall Street Journal, author of 'Woke Army' -- reports 54 organizations behind France's October protests: communist parties, revolutionary socialists, labor unions, Palestine-solidarity groups, international media. Twenty-eight communist and socialist youth organizations across 12 European countries are mobilizing for a November 20 walkout under the slogan "Fight for Our Future, Not Their Wars." Among the amplifiers: the network of Neville Roy Singham, the Marxist tech millionaire living in Shanghai -- Tricontinental, CodePink, BreakThrough News. The State Department casts it all as vindication of Secretary Rubio's July ministerial. Here is what holds, and what doesn't.

body:
Susan Collins has the backing she needs to hold this seat

Susan Collins has the backing she needs to hold this seat
| [](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.-3CcQ)
---
It's Karl Rove.I've spent decades in and around politics - advising presidents, running national campaigns, and watching hundreds of Senate races unfold from the inside. In all that time, I've learned to be careful about where I put my name and my energy. I don't back just anyone.But Susan Collins is different, Peter.I've watched her operate in the Senate for years, and what strikes me most isn't just her experience - it's her independence. She doesn't vote with a party out of habit. She studies the issue, talks to the people it affects, and makes the call she believes is right for Maine. That's rare in Washington today, and it's exactly why she's earned the trust of voters again and again.Right now, that independence and grit are being tested like never before. Troy Jackson and the Far-left machine behind him are pouring everything they have into flipping this seat because they know that if they take Maine, they take the Senate majority with it.Let me be blunt: this race will be one of the closest and most consequential in the country. It won't be decided by Maine alone. It will be decided by whether supporters in all 50 states step up the way they did for the races that mattered most in past cycles.That's why I'm writing to you directly today.Susan doesn't need a miracle. She needs steady, committed support from people like you who understand what's at stake - not just for Maine, but for the direction of the entire United States Senate. One seat can be the difference between a Senate that holds the line and one that hands total control to the Far-Left.I've seen races like this before. The ones who show up in these final, critical stretches are the ones who decide the outcome.[Can you join me and chip in today to help Susan finish strong?](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.)

Election Day has turned into Election Month. We're working to fix it.

| | | | [](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=dee2c8a855344f2585a4db195058d1ac&_e=W0EosFyIyu3UkLMl01Xzz7jNQSFBm99ZwzzXYJK94R5M6g0aaJMLqEMrWz_-YC8icTdy8sQrVpsR0FHnIQiBfhbnhmYVCX_QUfS0t6NepYmu3hy6FrqNs0IdfHSF0684DxDHseGIVRiP-XJVN93ukr8Yrp5imPJSJnGzYyEm6dcllv1mAhy786a3sVpaE4lag5VbXPObvbGVm4XApgdRoPYfsVcPzLkRn79CYc1qyppVE4R7ho_29iv0_ic08LtW5WKG_ivA_ZOiGczAAVsmx8_5fbnfnKYpCd6clOQE3P4AbA2dkbv-NvQ5H37ba6OlVzeGgn45QcwzwaQ6oKiO8Uh1FvVB_CZXA52AoV19o7hqAgPHe5F5Sx75ma0RItP53YWjfXjyNDjzdJRXQsWdaqNEyMTddVUjnD3E1hS5q-4fioqK09JmxAPHsE3dqSBf8jnPIDgAaZLX4QzwDJcq8TefXVLMy1YlC1j_60oz14FgQxS8xaT9K2_tPXYMjAZm9A0crMWYF-E1jfGRzi80Y-cR0egsoeTgHYMf4NhlD9NT7m8Og549fsay7OSCcrVfr8KKrOnGJYpsLdfp-5W3NC6l4cFOSq-2FNI50UDgJk05SuO-McSYP6hnz53C4nHuvcA9bx3j0m-SkGJGkhxzuOTlrxzULRp3Gyv6RJ5NeiDT51UP9LyhdYt0x-3JZZR4)

| | | Peter,
---
_Remember when Election Day was a single day?_ You went to your polling place, showed who you were, and cast your ballot. That night, the country turned on the news and found out who won. Somewhere along the way, **we lost that.** In a lot of states, voting now stretches across weeks of early and mail-in ballots. Ballots keep arriving in the mail for days after the polls close, and counties keep counting them. Races hang in limbo while the rest of the country waits and wonders what's going on. _And in many states, a voter can still cast a ballot without ever showing a photo ID._ I've seen this from the inside. I'm one of the election lawyers who started **Save Election Day** , and between us we've worked Election Nights and recounts more times than we can count. We keep coming back to the same conclusion: **the rules are the problem, and the rules can be changed.** **_So, we 're working to bring back Election Day!_****Save Election Day is taking President Trump 's election reforms to the states and fighting to make them law. Here's what we're fighting for:**
---
* Photo voter ID for every voter
* One national Election Day
* Every ballot in by the time the polls close
* Shorter windows for mail-in and early voting
* Only American citizens voting in American elections

---

Here's what most people miss. Elections in this country run on state law. Washington can debate election reform all it wants (and it has, for years), but the rules for how your ballot is cast and counted get written in statehouses. _The left figured that out a long time ago._ Their lawyers and activist groups have spent years in those statehouses stretching Election Day into Election Month. And we've seen from the inside how the left uses those long timelines to keep counting... and keep counting... until they win. We're a new organization, _and I won 't pretend otherwise. _**But we 're already working in states like Nevada and Ohio.** Most of our target legislatures reconvene this winter, and the bills we bring them are being written _now_. You went to your polling place, showed who you were, and cast your ballot. That night, the country turned on the news and found out who won. Somewhere along the way, we lost that. In a lot of states, voting now stretches across weeks of early and mail-in ballots. Ballots keep arriving in the mail for days after the polls close, and counties keep counting them. Races hang in limbo while the rest of the country waits and wonders what's going on. And in many states, a voter can still cast a ballot without ever showing a photo ID. I've seen this from the inside. I'm one of the election lawyers who started Save Election Day , and between us we've worked Election Nights and recounts more times than we can count. We keep coming back to the same conclusion: the rules are the problem, and the rules can be changed. So, we 're working to bring back Election Day!Save Election Day is taking President Trump 's election reforms to the states and fighting to make them law. Here's what we're fighting for: Photo voter ID for every voter One national Election Day Every ballot in by the time the polls close Shorter windows for mail-in and early voting Only American citizens voting in American elections Here's what most people miss. Elections in this country run on state law. Washington can debate election reform all it wants (and it has, for years), but the rules for how your ballot is cast and counted get written in statehouses. The left figured that out a long time ago. Their lawyers and activist groups have spent years in those statehouses stretching Election Day into Election Month. And we've seen from the inside how the left uses those long timelines to keep counting... and keep counting... until they win. We're a new organization, and I won 't pretend otherwise. But we 're already working in states like Nevada and Ohio. Most of our target legislatures reconvene this winter, and the bills we bring them are being written now. The groups on the other side are well funded and already organized, so we have to be too. Every election held under the old rules is another night when Americans go to bed not knowing who won. Your support will ensure we have the firepower to advocate and push these reforms through. | | | Thank you,Nicole Kelly Co-Founder and President Save Election Day P.S. Whatever happens on November 3rd, the fight to bring back Election Day will still be waiting the next morning. ** | | | ---|--- Contributions or gifts to Save Election Day are not tax deductible as charitable contributions. _**Cliff 's Note:**_
##### The House looks good. Really good. But the Senate is where Trump's agenda lives or dies, and right now it's sitting on a handful of races inside a single polling miss.
##### This week's _Midterm HQ_ walks through exactly which ones, what Democrats have to win, and what to watch in the early vote. Paid subscribers get the full dashboard and the Senate math.
##### [We're down to 10 days. _**-- Cliff**_
* * *
So let's get this straight. Democrats are crushing, but we still might not get what we're praying for out of these midterms?
Arrrgh, yes. On the one hand, this week:
* Structural indicators hit new lows for Trump, and new highs for Democrats.
* Democrats have a huge money advantage in the race for state legislative chambers, possibly as much as four times more than Republicans.
* The gubernatorial races continue to look good in most key races.
* And _The Cook Political Report_ now counts 220 US House seats as _at least_ "Lean" Democratic, with 17 more toss-ups. So as of today, the "chalk" result not only gives Democrats a majority but puts them on the doorstep of a big enough margin to withstand some factional infighting.

So why the hedging hesitation in the headline?
Because on the other hand, the Senate situation is resting on a knife's edge, as I'll get into below.

Over many town halls, forums, trips, debates, and voter outreach canvasses, I’ve seen Phil channel his _boundless_ energy into demonstrating that he will be a leader who shows up. He’s someone who will never back down from a chance to _fight like hell_ for what we all believe in: freedom, affordability, and opportunity.
**I can’t wait for him to serve as our next governor. And the reason this campaign has made it this far is because of you.**
You’ve put up yard signs. (If you’re like me, you’ve even put a campaign sticker on your go-to water bottle!)
You’ve spoken to your family, your friends, and your neighbors.
You’ve shown up to events.
You’ve taken the time to share your ideas for the Colorado Blueprint.
You’ve even knocked on doors or made phone calls!

You may have seen headlines bragging about record Republican super PAC money. The GOP's top Senate super PAC just raised a record $272.9 million in a single quarter. Here's what those headlines leave out: **a super PAC dollar doesn't go nearly as far as a candidate dollar.** Federal law requires TV and radio stations to sell ad time to candidates at their LOWEST UNIT RATE in the final 60 days before a general election. That's the same rate the station gives its best commercial customer. Super PACs don't get that rate. They pay whatever the station charges. | | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

name: Voto Latino
subject: Vote.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
We know this year has been difficult.
#
Peter, we know how hard this year has been for our community.
You can be angry. You _should_ be angry. But anger without a vote doesn’t change who controls Congress — or the Senate.
Anger doesn’t lower your grocery bill. It doesn’t stop ICE from showing up in your neighborhood. And it won’t bring separated families back together.
**Your vote on November 3rd will.**
It’s the most powerful tool we have to hold national Republicans accountable for what they’ve done to Latino communities.
That’s why Voto Latino is on the ground in every battleground state, knocking on doors, sharing accurate election information, and making sure every eligible Latino voter has what they need to show up and make their voice heard.
**[Peter, we only have 10 days left to make an impact. Will you chip in now to help us reach as many voters as possible before time runs out?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20261024-1.JrkLx1&amount=3&refcode=em20261024-712&t=1&akid=712%2E1366028%2E5aQ61a)**

Thirty-five generations ago, my ancestors built lives in the high desert of New Mexico. Growing up fishing with my dad and running through the desert with my cousins, I fell in love with New Mexico’s natural wonders and learned that we all have a responsibility to care for our planet.
_Since my childhood, I have seen the impacts of climate change on New Mexico._
That’s why, when I was elected to Congress, I fought to protect sacred lands. As Secretary of the Interior, I helped the Biden administration protect more land and water than any administration in U.S. history while also creating good jobs in clean energy and conservation and cleaning up legacy pollution.
**But now all of that progress is at risk.**
Donald Trump and his MAGA allies have worked to gut environmental protections and sell off public lands — all while New Mexico stands on the front lines of the devastating impacts of climate change.
Governors are the first line of defense against the Trump agenda, especially when it comes to standing up against the brazen attacks on our environment. **And as Governor, I will be a fierce defender of our home, but I can’t win this race on my own.**
Republicans have already spent big to stop us because they care more about money than about protecting New Mexico’s families and the beautiful public lands we call home. **[So if you’re with me, friend, I’m personally asking: Will you please chip in $5 today to help power my victory in November so I can protect New Mexico’s land, water, and future?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17378?refcode=jtk1659-fr-nd&t=8&akid=13399%2E400544%2ErGMTs8)**
Thank you for doing your part to protect New Mexico for future generations.

Be fierce,

— Deb

Peter,
Trump's weaponized DOJ is rolling out its first major intervention in the midterm election two weeks out from Election Day in California, attempting to invalidate ~20,000 alleged "noncitizen" voters.
First, the facts: DOJ is asking federal judges to halt the counting of thousands of ballots until voters' citizenship can be verified. This is a fishing expedition at best, and at worst an obvious attempt to gain a foothold toward declaring all of CA's elections "invalid" and cancelling even more ballots.
An LA County election official said that a sample of the 20k records at issue showed most of the people identified already had cancelled registrations; and of the others, a small number were mailed ballots (implying they were valid voters). Most of them had never voted.
Next, the truth: This is not about rooting out invalid or illegal voters. DOJ is already able to investigate and prosecute any fraudulent voting or noncitizen voters. States routinely cooperate with legal requests on specific cases.
It is about using the power and might of the federal government's top law enforcement agency to intimidate election officials, erode public trust in elections, and add another note to the fictional narrative Trump has created that fraudulent voting is widespread--even though no one can prove it.

Defend Our Courts is investing in the voter education needed to combat the Right's disinformation machine which is now routinely given new ammunition by our own government.
We are fighting to save key state Supreme Court seats that will be crucial to protecting the outcome of the election after all the votes are cast.
And we are turning out as many pro-democracy voters as we can in the final weeks of this election in swing states across the country to make this midterm election too big to rig.

First, the facts: DOJ is asking federal judges to halt the counting of thousands of ballots until voters' citizenship can be verified. This is a fishing expedition at best, and at worst an obvious attempt to gain a foothold toward declaring all of CA's elections "invalid" and cancelling even more ballots. An LA County election official said that a sample of the 20k records at issue showed most of the people identified already had cancelled registrations; and of the others, a small number were mailed ballots (implying they were valid voters). body:
News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.
| | | | |
---
| A message from Congressional District 2 Candidate Brinker Harding...
---
| Fellow Republicans, Two years ago, this seat was decided by fewer than two points, and this year will be just as close. Denise Powell's answer to everything is another tax. She'd have let the largest tax increase since World War II take a bite out of your paycheck, and she'd keep taxing the Social Security you spent a lifetime earning. Her campaign runs on dark money, and her values are just as far from home. I believe you know how to spend your money better than Washington does, and I've governed that way. On the City Council, we balanced the budget every year and cut the property tax levy three times, keeping more money in your pocket. I'll bring that same discipline to Congress and make Washington answer to you. Please make a plan to vote, whether that's early in person or on Election Day. Remind your friends and family to vote as well, close races are won one conversation at a time. Brinker Harding
---
| Letter from the Chair...
---
| Friends,
Eleven days. This is not the time to tap the brakes. This is the time to push the gas pedal to the floor. Out-of-state money is pouring into Nebraska for Denise Powell and Dan Osborn, and the Left is betting Republicans will get comfortable and coast to the finish line. We can't let that happen. Every race on this ballot, from the U.S. Senate down to the power board, comes down to who shows up and who brings their neighbors with them.
The choice in front of Nebraskans could not be clearer. Democrats want bigger government, more spending, and more decisions made in Washington by people who have never set foot in our state. We believe Nebraskans know how to run their own lives, their own businesses, and their own families. They fought voter ID. We passed it. They want to keep feeding a system that sends tax bills higher every year. They want to tell your kids what to think. We want parents in charge of their children's education and our girls protected in their own sports.
So let's finish this. If you've already voted, thank you. Now call three people this weekend and make sure they vote too. If your mail ballot is still on the counter, drop it off at your county election office or drop box instead of mailing it this late. Early voting is open at your county election office through November 2, and polls are open Tuesday, November 3. Bring your photo ID. And if you can spare a few hours, knock on one more neighborhood or make one more round of calls.
We did not come this far to fall short at the finish line. Eleven days. Foot on the gas. Let's bring it home.

Together we win!
In Liberty and in Truth,
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

Five women. One moment to make history.
Five women. One moment to make history.

| | Peter, Something is happening this November that has never happened in American history: Three Indigenous women are running for top statewide offices in the same year. And a fourth is defending the seat where she made history in 2018. **Mary Peltola** , a Yup’ik leader and the first Alaska Native ever elected to Congress, is challenging Republican Senator Dan Sullivan and just outpolled him in Alaska’s primary. **Peggy Flanagan** , a citizen of the White Earth Nation, won her primary by roughly 20 points. If she wins in November, she’ll be the first Native American woman ever to serve in the U.S. Senate. **Deb Haaland** , a citizen of Laguna Pueblo and the first Native American Cabinet secretary, won her primary with more than 70% of the vote. She would be the first Native American woman ever elected governor. **Sharice Davids** , a citizen of the Ho-Chunk Nation and one of the first two Native American women ever elected to Congress, is defending her Kansas seat after winning her primary with 83%. **Claire Valdez,** a citizen of the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo Nation and a union organizer serving in the New York State Assembly, won her primary in New York’s 7th District this June — and is now poised to grow Indigenous representation in Congress. Here’s the thing: all five are tied or ahead in their races. But leading a poll isn’t even remotely the same as winning on Election Day. The final stretch is the expensive part, and that’s why Indigenous Women Lead PAC exists — to close the funding gaps and make sure these women cross the finish line. clean_body: Five women. One moment to make history. Five women. One moment to make history. | ~~ | | Peter, Something is happening this November that has never happened in American history: Three Indigenous women are running for top statewide offices in the same year. And a fourth is defending the seat where she made history in 2018. Mary Peltola , a Yup’ik leader and the first Alaska Native ever elected to Congress, is challenging Republican Senator Dan Sullivan and just outpolled him in Alaska’s primary. Peggy Flanagan , a citizen of the White Earth Nation, won her primary by roughly 20 points. If she wins in November, she’ll be the first Native American woman ever to serve in the U.S. Senate. Deb Haaland , a citizen of Laguna Pueblo and the first Native American Cabinet secretary, won her primary with more than 70% of the vote. She would be the first Native American woman ever elected governor. Sharice Davids , a citizen of the Ho-Chunk Nation and one of the first two Native American women ever elected to Congress, is defending her Kansas seat after winning her primary with 83%. Claire Valdez, a citizen of the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo Nation and a union organizer serving in the New York State Assembly, won her primary in New York’s 7th District this June — and is now poised to grow Indigenous representation in Congress. Here’s the thing: all five are tied or ahead in their races. But leading a poll isn’t even remotely the same as winning on Election Day. The final stretch is the expensive part, and that’s why Indigenous Women Lead PAC exists — to close the funding gaps and make sure these women cross the finish line. ~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | ~~ Representation matters, and this year, it’s on the ballot. Non-Contribution Account (For TPPAC, Inc.’s Expenditures Other Than Direct Contributions to Federal Committees)

As permitted by law, TPPAC, Inc. maintains a non-contribution account for the purpose of influencing federal, state, and local elections. Federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the name, address, occupation, and employer of individuals whose contribution exceeds $200 in an election cycle. For contributions from federal committees, corporations, and labor unions - regardless of contribution amount - federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the committee’s name and address. State and local law may require us to collect and report additional information.

Contributions to this account may be used to influence federal elections by making independent expenditures in support of or in opposition to federal candidates. Additionally, in state and local jurisdictions that permit non-individual type (e.g., corporate) contributions directly to candidates and/or committees, contributions to this account may be used for both independent expenditures and direct contributions to candidates and/or committees, as permitted by state and local law.

body:
A 45-million-acre corporate land grab

| | | | Peter, How do you successfully execute a 45-million-acre corporate land grab? **Step one:** You take an executive who spent his career lobbying to chop down national forests. **Step two:** You appoint him as the Chief of the U.S. Forest Service. Step three: You wait for him to open the floodgates. **That is exactly what is happening right now in Washington.** Tom Schultz is the first-ever Forest Service Chief who didn't actually come from within the agency. Before this, he was the president of a timber trade association. Now, he is using his government authority to completely kill the 25-year-old "roadless rule," stripping protections from 45 million acres of untouched wilderness so his former employers can bulldoze roads and clear-cut the backcountry. The politicians rubber-stamping this heist are looking the American public in the eye and claiming they need to build logging roads into pristine habitats to "prevent wildfires." It is complete garbage. [**This is a 45-million-acre heist happening in broad daylight. Will you pitch in $10 today to our rapid-response war chest so we can expose this corruption?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/xfWVi21zo0_Hgz2t4K_YsA~~/AAUS1hA~/s8BFvpzra9s5w1YizlgAeE3YuKt-Pn_9369Uf0ICMdlfkfu6su_aQ3kqqP6sQaFNYcmepCAU6wcnm8tX58LUMKYAhIkesYZjksPpSzRyV3-tRxG_mUW7XvJC2k7JSlwSyYOSRcLMZD3wK4hZ2gQW2bcThDx1iRkuAWDg1tp-C4OSEyL4TJTVBcAIQqKuFk0dMAl9w-pMPk371pD6Nbzhodl1hFUdCP4qLo_uQpEa1GAoapa_fL-uhzS8PszPSoH_E0nOfGXB7BfjwUvA5ePA9h5KB6MrJHdpVLIjpgMNf67SgGLvoL6mFIXuG3l_HFv7QYoq_n5iqyZx6yfMPbXF8l4UoF0jCRxPAqKPmSjuGLY~) The Forest Service's _own data_ shows that wildfires are nearly three times as likely to start near roads because they bring in human ignition sources. They aren't trying to stop forest fires—they are using the threat of fires as a human shield for the timber lobby. And the lumber executives know it. They are literally bragging on corporate earnings calls, telling their Wall Street investors, "We know the new Forest Service chief." Schultz and the politicians enabling him think they can quietly liquidate the last remaining old-growth forests in America without facing any consequences. name: Deb Haaland
subject: We've worked too hard and come too far to slow down now.
body:
There's too much at stake to leave anything to chance.
Peter, we have just 10 days until Election Day, and I want you to know one thing: _**I'm leaving it all on the field.**_
[](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261024-3.mhfbaw&refcode=em-20261024-3&t=1&akid=2185%2E1086043%2E5nlLU1)
We've worked too hard and come too far to slow down now. **But this race is far from over.** Fox News has called this race a top pickup opportunity for Republicans, and they’ll stop at nothing to flip this seat red -- _especially now that new polling shows this race is “within striking distance”._
**[There's too much at stake to leave anything to chance. Will you split a donation of $5 between Wes Moore and my campaign today to help us reach every voter across New Mexico and win this race?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261024-3.mhfbaw&refcode=em-20261024-3&t=2&akid=2185%2E1086043%2E5nlLU1)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261024-3.mhfbaw&amount=5&refcode=em-20261024-3&t=3&akid=2185%2E1086043%2E5nlLU1)**
Wes Moore and I are both fighting to lower costs, strengthen our public schools, protect access to healthcare, and create good-paying jobs for New Mexicans and Marylanders. But none of that happens unless we both win on November 3.
That's why over these final 10 days, I'm giving this campaign everything I've got. Every conversation, every community, every voter we can reach. _And I'm asking you to do the same._
We have a real opportunity to make history in New Mexico, Peter. Let's make sure we give it everything we've got. **[Will you split a donation of $5 or however much you can spare between Wes Moore and my campaign today to help us finish this race strong and win on November 3?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261024-3.mhfbaw&refcode=em-20261024-3&t=4&akid=2185%2E1086043%2E5nlLU1)**

Be fierce,
Deb

clean_body: There's too much at stake to leave anything to chance. Peter, we have just 10 days until Election Day, and I want you to know one thing: I'm leaving it all on the field. We've worked too hard and come too far to slow down now. But this race is far from over. Fox News has called this race a top pickup opportunity for Republicans, and they’ll stop at nothing to flip this seat red -- especially now that new polling shows this race is “within striking distance”. Wes Moore and I are both fighting to lower costs, strengthen our public schools, protect access to healthcare, and create good-paying jobs for New Mexicans and Marylanders. But none of that happens unless we both win on November 3. That's why over these final 10 days, I'm giving this campaign everything I've got. Every conversation, every community, every voter we can reach. And I'm asking you to do the same. We have a real opportunity to make history in New Mexico, Peter. Let's make sure we give it everything we've got. Be fierce, Deb

Every door we knocked, every ad we ran, every stand we took against the radical left, we did together, because people like you believed North Texas was worth fighting for. Now we are down to the final hours, the House hangs by a thread, and the radical left is favored to take it. Everything is on the line. I am asking you to do the same, one last time. | | Whatever happens, thank you for standing with me. Let's finish this the right way. | | Beth Van Duyne ---|--- | PAID FOR BY BETH VAN DUYNE FOR CONGRESS

| | | Fellow Voter,
---
_Remember when Election Day was a single day?_ You went to your polling place, showed who you were, and cast your ballot. That night, the country turned on the news and found out who won. Somewhere along the way, **we lost that.** In a lot of states, voting now stretches across weeks of early and mail-in ballots. Ballots keep arriving in the mail for days after the polls close, and counties keep counting them. Races hang in limbo while the rest of the country waits and wonders what's going on. _And in many states, a voter can still cast a ballot without ever showing a photo ID._ I've seen this from the inside. I'm one of the election lawyers who started **Save Election Day** , and between us we've worked Election Nights and recounts more times than we can count. We keep coming back to the same conclusion: **the rules are the problem, and the rules can be changed.** **_So, we 're working to bring back Election Day!_****Save Election Day is taking President Trump 's election reforms to the states and fighting to make them law. Here's what we're fighting for:**
---
* Photo voter ID for every voter
* One national Election Day
* Every ballot in by the time the polls close
* Shorter windows for mail-in and early voting
* Only American citizens voting in American elections

There's a moment that now happens every autumn Saturday somewhere in America. A starting quarterback trots to the sideline in the third quarter of a two-score game, nursing an ankle no trainer can see from the couch. The betting line had moved four points overnight. The backup hands off nine straight times into a wall. And in living rooms from Birmingham to Boise, a hundred thousand amateur auditors put down the wings and begin the forensic accounting.
Nobody in those rooms has evidence. Nobody needs it. The appearance is the verdict, and it arrives before the fourth-quarter TV timeout.
We have legalized this feeling. Forty states and counting take bets on every snap, every free throw, every garbage-time layup, which means every strange sequence now has a dollar sign attached and a customer with a receipt. The line moving isn't a rumor anymore; it's a market with a timestamp. So the fans do what fans do: they convict on vibes and rarely apologize.
Here is the uncomfortable part. Last January, federal prosecutors suggested the barstool was underpricing it. Twenty current and former college players, seventeen Division I schools, roughly twenty-nine games manipulated across two seasons -- the largest point-shaving case since Boston College, 1978. The FBI's big score came from the hardwood, not the gridiron, but nobody who watched October believes the turf is cleaner.
The grain of this country's distrust has a new ring pattern, and it is made of legal sportsbook logos. Once "rigged" becomes your prior, an honest game reads as a fixed one. That's the tax.
Now take the same instinct -- the fan who notices -- and point it at the two institutions Americans are told to trust with the slow things: a state supreme court and the federal agency that pays the doctors.
**The bench investigates itself**
Start in Colorado, because the documents are old enough to have a birthday...

See, Cotham was elected as a Democrat. Then in 2023 she switched parties, handing Republicans a veto-proof supermajority in the North Carolina House on a silver platter, and cast the deciding vote to restrict abortion access across the state.
And now, the North Carolina GOP are only one seat away from regaining a veto-proof supermajority. **When I talk about how vital it is that we build Democratic power at the state legislative level, this situation is precisely why.** We have to invest in expanding majorities and picking up seats in red states so that one vote isn’t all that stands in the way of the GOP’s radical agenda.

Ken made history as one of the youngest elected officials in North Carolina at just 21 years old. As Mayor Pro Tem of Matthews, he expanded affordable housing, secured the largest park investment in a generation, and helped bring high paying jobs to the region.
That’s exactly the kind of bold young leader this district deserves — someone who will truly show up and deliver for his constituents.
Winning Ken’s race is absolutely critical to protecting the Democratic governor’s veto power. Republicans are just one seat away from a veto-proof supermajority in the House, which would let them override the governor on everything from affordable housing to healthcare.

We have to invest in expanding majorities and picking up seats in red states so that one vote isn’t all that stands in the way of the GOP’s radical agenda. And with just 10 days until Election Day, we have a real chance to flip Tricia Cotham’s seat blue and stop Republicans from gaining a veto-proof super-majority in North Carolina. That’s why I’m so fired up about Ken McCool. Ken made history as one of the youngest elected officials in North Carolina at just 21 years old. As Mayor Pro Tem of Matthews, he expanded affordable housing, secured the largest park investment in a generation, and helped bring high paying jobs to the region. That’s exactly the kind of bold young leader this district deserves — someone who will truly show up and deliver for his constituents. Winning Ken’s race is absolutely critical to protecting the Democratic governor’s veto power. Republicans are just one seat away from a veto-proof supermajority in the House, which would let them override the governor on everything from affordable housing to healthcare. District 105 is competitive, but it’s winnable — and Ken is exactly the candidate to take it all the way. He just needs us to have his back in these final days. Thank you, David Hogg

In 2018, we backed candidates who were just getting started. Look at them now:
* **Abigail Spanberger:** A former U.S. postal inspector and CIA operations officer who spent nearly a decade working counterterrorism and national security cases before flipping a House seat in Virginia in 2018. Last November, she made history as Virginia's first woman governor.
* **Mikie Sherrill:** A U.S. Naval Academy graduate and Navy helicopter pilot who spent nearly a decade on active duty flying Sea King helicopter missions across Europe and the Middle East, including during the Iraq War, before flipping a House seat in New Jersey in a highly competitive 2018 race. In 2025, she was elected as the state's governor.
* **Elissa Slotkin:** A former CIA analyst who deployed on three tours to Iraq alongside the U.S. military before working national security roles at the Pentagon and White House. After flipping a House seat in Michigan in 2018, Elissa served three terms before winning a U.S. Senate seat in 2024.

This year, EMILYs List is again supporting a robust group of House candidates who spent years — and in some cases decades — serving in uniform before seeking elected office:
* **JoAnna Mendoza:** A retired Marine Corps drill instructor turned veterans' advocate who is running to flip Arizona's 6th Congressional District and beat Rep. Juan Ciscomani.
* **Jessica Killin:** An Army veteran and fourth-generation Colorado native who is taking on Rep. Jeff Crank in a bid to flip Colorado's 5th Congressional District.
* **Leela Gray:** A retired Army brigadier general and attorney who is challenging Rep. Anna Paulina Luna and making Florida's Republican-leaning 13th Congressional District competitive for the first time in years.
* **Nancy Lacore:** A retired three-star Navy admiral and former chief of Navy Reserve, removed from her post by MAGA extremist Pete Hegseth during a partisan Pentagon leadership shakeup, now running to flip South Carolina's 1st Congressional District.
* **Rebecca Bennett:** A former Navy helicopter pilot and test pilot turned healthcare executive who won her crowded primary and is running to flip New Jersey's 7th Congressional District and beat Rep. Tom Kean Jr.
* **Cait Conley:** An Army special operations veteran and former White House counterterrorism director who is challenging Trump-endorsed Rep. Mike Lawler to flip New York's 17th Congressional District.
* **Kristina Knickerbocker:** An Air Force veteran and neuro-oncology nurse practitioner running against longtime incumbent Rep. Mike Turner in Ohio's 10th Congressional District.
* **Elaine Luria:** A retired 20-year Navy commander and former two-term congresswoman seeking a rematch against Rep. Jen Kiggans to reclaim her seat in Virginia's 2nd Congressional District.

Different branches. Different careers. Different parts of the country. But each of these women entered politics after already spending years in service to the country.
This election is about more than reclaiming power from the Trump administration — it's about changing who holds that power in the first place. That's the mission EMILYs List has always carried out: recruiting, supporting, and electing women who get real results and build a better future for all of us.

clean_body: EMILYs List is building the bench. | = Peter, In 2018, EMILYs List-endorsed women flipped 24 Republican-held seats in the U.S. House — singlehandedly delivering Democrats the majority. That class included women who came to politics after careers in the military, intelligence, and national security. Republicans were certain they'd hold on to their majority that year. They were wrong. And this year, we have the chance to do it again. = | = In 2018, we backed candidates who were just getting started. Look at them now: Abigail Spanberger: A former U.S. postal inspector and CIA operations officer who spent nearly a decade working counterterrorism and national security cases before flipping a House seat in Virginia in 2018. Last November, she made history as Virginia's first woman governor. Mikie Sherrill: A U.S. Naval Academy graduate and Navy helicopter pilot who spent nearly a decade on active duty flying Sea King helicopter missions across Europe and the Middle East, including during the Iraq War, before flipping a House seat in New Jersey in a highly competitive 2018 race. In 2025, she was elected as the state's governor. Elissa Slotkin: A former CIA analyst who deployed on three tours to Iraq alongside the U.S. military before working national security roles at the Pentagon and White House. After flipping a House seat in Michigan in 2018, Elissa served three terms before winning a U.S. Senate seat in 2024. This year, EMILYs List is again supporting a robust group of House candidates who spent years — and in some cases decades — serving in uniform before seeking elected office: JoAnna Mendoza: A retired Marine Corps drill instructor turned veterans' advocate who is running to flip Arizona's 6th Congressional District and beat Rep. Juan Ciscomani. Jessica Killin: An Army veteran and fourth-generation Colorado native who is taking on Rep. Jeff Crank in a bid to flip Colorado's 5th Congressional District. Leela Gray: A retired Army brigadier general and attorney who is challenging Rep. Anna Paulina Luna and making Florida's Republican-leaning 13th Congressional District competitive for the first time in years. Nancy Lacore: A retired three-star Navy admiral and former chief of Navy Reserve, removed from her post by MAGA extremist Pete Hegseth during a partisan Pentagon leadership shakeup, now running to flip South Carolina's 1st Congressional District. Rebecca Bennett: A former Navy helicopter pilot and test pilot turned healthcare executive who won her crowded primary and is running to flip New Jersey's 7th Congressional District and beat Rep. Tom Kean Jr. Cait Conley: An Army special operations veteran and former White House counterterrorism director who is challenging Trump-endorsed Rep. Mike Lawler to flip New York's 17th Congressional District. Kristina Knickerbocker: An Air Force veteran and neuro-oncology nurse practitioner running against longtime incumbent Rep. Mike Turner in Ohio's 10th Congressional District. Elaine Luria: A retired 20-year Navy commander and former two-term congresswoman seeking a rematch against Rep. Jen Kiggans to reclaim her seat in Virginia's 2nd Congressional District. Different branches. Different careers. Different parts of the country. But each of these women entered politics after already spending years in service to the country. This election is about more than reclaiming power from the Trump administration — it's about changing who holds that power in the first place. clean_body: | | | | | | | Folks – my friend, LG Ghazala Hashmi, asked me to reach out with an update as we near Election Day.= = I’ve been in public service a long time now, and frankly, I’ve never seen anything like the second Trump term. Did you ever think we’d see a president openly attack the free press, spread wild conspiracy theories about our elections, and use taxpayer dollars to run blatantly partisan political ads ahead of an election? Did you ever think we’d see a president blatantly profit off the presidency – enriching himself, his family, and his allies while working families get squeezed? Did you ever think we’d have GOP majorities in Congress that strip health care access from millions of Americans and shutter rural clinics to pay for massive tax breaks for the very wealthy? Folks, I first got into public service because I believed in a simple idea: that everyone deserves the same shot as success I was lucky enough to have. That means expanding access to health care and lowering costs for working families. It means making it easier to afford a first home and start a family. It means preparing our communities, economy, and national security for the changes brought on by Artificial Intelligence. And it means putting a real check on this administration run amok. Election Day is just 10 days away – and frankly, control of Congress could come down to what happens here in Virginia. If we have any chance of electing Democratic majorities that will fight for working families and stand up to this president and his acolytes, we need to win BIG here in the Commonwealth. = = The fight continues, Mark Warner = | | | = | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- | | | Email us: info@nextchapterpac.org This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Even as our judicial system attempts to hold him accountable, Donald Trump has continued his persistent assault on the core pillars of our democracy.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5531fda0-4874-4a15-9814-c6dcaa8b1f13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is awful, un-American, and unacceptable. But it also reveals a silver lining: **Trump is terrified of the Blue Wave on the horizon.**
Democrats across the nation are crushing the polls and are on track to flip the Senate - and this race is no exception.
The Republican establishment never saw this coming - this election is our best chance in a generation to flip Kentucky blue.
That's why Trump showed up to "deep-red" Kentucky to prop up my flailing opponent, Andy Barr.
That's why a MAGA-aligned super PAC is dumping $5 million into attack ads against me.
I've been outspent before. In my primary, I was outraised roughly five to one, and we won anyway.
We didn't have the money. We had the people: from the hood to the holler, across race, partisanship, and class, Kentuckians who were tired of being cheated stepped up to join this movement.
_We 'll never match them dollar-for-dollar, but the strength of this grassroots movement is palpable._
There are just 10 days until Election Day. Every attack ad that goes unanswered is a vote we could lose. So I'm asking you directly: will you chip in $25 right now to keep us in the fight against Trump and his super PAC allies?
[Chip in to my Senate Campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/5531fda0-4874-4a15-9814-c6dcaa8b1f13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Make a recurring donation](https://substack.com/redirect/ef4e5768-0a92-4538-858c-b1aad885a01a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Together,
_Charles Booker_

### About Kristin Hook
Kristin is running to fight for affordability, opportunity, and accountability for working families like her own. | | | Randy is running in a **_critical_** swing district in this year’s midterm election. In fact, the _Los Angeles Times_ recently reported that CA-22 is the **_only_** race in California currently considered a true toss-up. But I want you to know **_why_****** Randy is running. Randy is the son of Mexican immigrants. He grew up in Bakersfield, where he shared a bunk bed in the living room with his brothers. He watched his older brother navigate life as a DACA recipient, while his younger brother put on a Marine uniform and served our country. And he became the first person in his family to go to college. That first-generation experience shaped the person Randy is today. He became a community college professor and school board trustee to ensure that young people in the Central Valley had more opportunities. But that wasn’t enough. He kept seeing families in his community struggle with healthcare, housing, immigration, and poor air quality. Eventually, Randy decided he couldn’t just watch from the sidelines. He decided to run for Congress. Now he is taking on incumbent Republican David Valadao in CA-22, a district where the outcome could decide who controls the House. I wanted you to know Randy’s story because I believe it matters who we send to Washington. Someone with Randy’s experiences brings something different to public service. He knows what it means to worry about whether your family can afford healthcare. He knows what it means to be the first in your family to go to college. He knows what it means to build a life in a community that too often feels overlooked. clean_body: Randy Villegas, the Democratic nominee for California’s 22nd District. | | | = | | Peter, I want to introduce you to someone I’m proud to support: = | | | = | | | Randy is running in a critical swing district in this year’s midterm election. In fact, the Los Angeles Times recently reported that CA-22 is the only race in California currently considered a true toss-up. But I want you to know why** Randy is running. Randy is the son of Mexican immigrants. He grew up in Bakersfield, where he shared a bunk bed in the living room with his brothers. He watched his older brother navigate life as a DACA recipient, while his younger brother put on a Marine uniform and served our country. And he became the first person in his family to go to college. That first-generation experience shaped the person Randy is today. He became a community college professor and school board trustee to ensure that young people in the Central Valley had more opportunities. But that wasn’t enough. He kept seeing families in his community struggle with healthcare, housing, immigration, and poor air quality. Eventually, Randy decided he couldn’t just watch from the sidelines. He decided to run for Congress. Now he is taking on incumbent Republican David Valadao in CA-22, a district where the outcome could decide who controls the House. I wanted you to know Randy’s story because I believe it matters who we send to Washington. Someone with Randy’s experiences brings something different to public service. He knows what it means to worry about whether your family can afford healthcare. He knows what it means to be the first in your family to go to college. He knows what it means to build a life in a community that too often feels overlooked. I’m proud to help make sure more people know who he is. = | | | = = = | | = = = | | In this together, Maxine | | | = | | Maxine Dexter is a critical care physician with decades of experience using facts and following science to help her patients. Now she's using those skills in Congress to ensure healthy communities by standing up to Big Pharma, fighting climate change, and expanding reproductive rights, as well as rebuilding a fair economy for all by protecting Social Security and Medicare. body:
|
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142111019/655829897/-664395954?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS84OTkxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODkwOTBhMi1kMGNmLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1qFTCbG1EGGCkDib6xCssiT4Otj77OTpvU3LfdMvfNo=)

name: Wes Moore
subject: A conversation like that one
body:
What I said
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2183%2E1086043%2ER-NRaU)
A few weeks ago, I sat down for Jubilee’s _Surrounded_ and debated with 20 people who had not voted in the last election.
**The cynics out there in the world tell us a conversation like the one I had isn’t worth having.** That we’ve become too divided. That everyone has already chosen a side, and the only thing left to do is shout louder than our political opponents.
But that isn’t what I saw in that room. And I do not think it is true in this country. We haven’t crossed a threshold where we can no longer listen to one another or to work together.
The year that we celebrated America’s 250th anniversary, I’m struck by the fact that our nation’s story has never been one of perfection. It’s one of progress. Generation after generation, Americans have chosen to do their part in expanding the promise of this country.
That work has never been automatic. It has always required participation from people who believe that tomorrow can be better than today.
**[If you share that belief with me, I would appreciate a donation to our re-election campaign today so we can continue our work.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261024-2.JqVhFQ&refcode=em-20261024-2&t=2&akid=2183%2E1086043%2ER-NRaU)**
I did not go into _Surrounded_ – or write this – to shame people who have opted out of the system.
Quite the contrary. I understand that choice.
I don’t come from a political background. When I ran for office the first time a few years ago, I had to convince many of my family members to vote for me. It’s not like we aren’t cool. They just don’t rush to the ballot box every year.
It struck me that people I love – people who cared deeply about their communities and their country – had been absent from a democratic act that generations of Americans fought for.
Somewhere along the way, they stopped believing that politics had much to do with them – or that anyone in politics had much interest in them. That realization has stayed with me. And it is exactly why I did _Surrounded._
Democracy is a relationship. Those who have the privilege of serving in government share a responsibility to give people a reason to believe their participation counts. To earn their trust. To show the public that government is not something that happens to us, but something we have the power to shape. As an elected official, I take that responsibility seriously. It’s sacred, and essential.
If those of us in public office do our jobs right, then voting becomes about more than casting a ballot. It is an act of hope.
If we’re serious about strengthening democracy over the next 250 years, we cannot only invest in elections. _We have to invest in one another._ The work of patriotism is not passive, and it is not performative. It is service.
Real patriotism asks us to see our humanity in each other before we see our differences. It asks us to remember that the future of this country has always depended on ordinary people doing extraordinary things together – not because they agreed on everything, but because they believed this nation was worth building together, despite our disagreements.
**[If you’re with me, and you believe in what we’re building together, can you chip in any amount to our campaign today?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261024-2.JqVhFQ&refcode=em-20261024-2&t=3&akid=2183%2E1086043%2ER-NRaU)**
My final challenge is a simple one: Sit down with people in your life and in your community who disagree with you. Have honest conversations. Listen. You may be surprised by what you find. And you may even end up working together to make a big difference in our world.
Elevate,
Wes

name: Mark Kelly
subject: It was a tough call
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
body:
It was uncharted territory, but I had to figure out what I was going to do.
#

Friend, it’s Mark.
Last November, Trump and Hegseth came after me with everything they had. They tried to take my rank and my pension, they tried to get me arrested and federally indicted, and Trump even said I should be hanged.
There’s no contingency for that kind of thing, no playbook. It was uncharted territory, but I had to figure out what I was going to do. So, I looked at my options, and Gabby and I made a decision. I was going to sue the Secretary of Defense.
That wasn’t an easy call. I spent my entire life serving this country, and I ended up facing down the full weight of the Executive Branch. A federal judge ruled in my favor in that case. He rejected Hegseth’s arguments, but almost as soon as the judge ruled, Hegseth appealed.
Since the ruling on that appeal didn’t come in September, we’re expecting it next year. But, here’s the thing: It’s impossible to know for sure. We’ll find out about that ruling at the same time as everybody else, and when it comes we need to be ready.
[**I’m humbly asking you to make a donation because all of this is far from over. Anything helps, and it all goes towards combatting Trump wherever we can.**](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-oct26.SGbrxo&refcode=em261024-1-MS&t=1&akid=6785%2E6688874%2EGg81Qe)

Just 10 days from now, Americans will decide whether the U.S. Senate keeps rubber-stamping Donald Trump's agenda or finally puts up some resistance.
**It all comes down to whether we can flip the Senate blue.**
I've served in this chamber long enough to see how much the people we elect matter when it comes to what gets done. The people we elect to the Senate will determine who gets confirmed to run the Pentagon or sit on the Supreme Court, which bills ever reach a vote, and whether anyone in Washington is willing to ask the tough questions of people like RFK Jr. and Pete Hegseth.
So I want to walk you through where the fight for the Senate actually stands today - and I'm hoping you'll join us.
**Here 's the landscape we're looking at:**
As we've gotten closer to Election Day, more and more voters have turned away from Trump. They're less willing to back an agenda that leaves them with higher bills and less money to pay them with while Trump uses the money to line his pockets and put our service members in harm's way.
So Democrats are offering an alternative: We need to make things like healthcare and housing more affordable. We need to put money back in folks' wallets, and we need to end Trump's ill-conceived, unjustified forever war in Iran.
**The best and last chance we have to put a real check on Trump 's agenda is by flipping the Senate in 10 days.** But to do that, Democrats have three important seats we need to defend, and we must flip four Republican-held seats.
I won't sugarcoat it: That's a tall order.
Democrats need to keep Georgia, Michigan, and New Hampshire blue.
And Democrats need to flip four of the following:
* Alaska
* Kansas
* Maine
* Iowa
* North Carolina
* Ohio
* Texas

Senate control runs through states Democrats haven't won in years, so I won't pretend this is an easy map.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/af45e273-15c8-4223-9544-d3bd5d1e0501?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But, I will say, Democrats have made _incredible_ progress few could have predicted a year ago - particularly in Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, and Texas.
Think about it: A year ago, if you'd told someone Democrats would be fighting for Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, and Texas a week and a half out from Election Day, they'd have laughed.
But now, polls are showing Democrats making HUGE gains in these states!
This is what a movement looks like. This is what your grassroots donations and energy have made possible.
**So we can 't take this for granted, and we can't get ahead of ourselves. We have to fight for every seat.**
Ultimately, Senate control will be fought and won seat by seat. Media outlets and pundits aren't in charge of the outcome - voters are. And we have to do everything we can to reach every single voter in these last few days. What decides these races in the final stretch is whether candidates can keep their ads on the air, keep their field programs running, and get people to the polls.
Republicans and their billionaire megadonors know this, and they are pouring everything they have into these states to shut us down. Democrats don't have the same slate of megadonors. We have something better: YOU. The margin between a Senate that can stand up to this administration and one that can't is supported by grassroots donors, chipping in what they can, when they can, one gift at a time.
We've seen the havoc wreaked by the Trump administration for too many long years now. We've watched what happens when the people in charge face no consequences, but we've also seen what becomes possible when there are enough Democrats willing to stand up and demand better.
A Democratic Senate would mean real oversight. It would mean a chance to block unqualified extremists from being confirmed to Cabinet and judicial positions. It means that when this administration puts our service members at risk or lets bigotry pass without consequence, we're in a powerful position to speak out and fight back.
**So I 'm asking you directly: **If you've been waiting for the moment to join this movement, now is the time. This is it. The final few days. If you've already given to take back the Senate, thank you. If you're on the fence, take it from me: There is no better time.
**[If you chip in right now, you'll help show Republicans that our candidates in these battleground states have what it takes to run through the finish line and declare victory on election night.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/af45e273-15c8-4223-9544-d3bd5d1e0501?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Every dollar matters because these gifts add up fast when thousands of us take action together.
[Donate Now](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/af45e273-15c8-4223-9544-d3bd5d1e0501?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We have 10 days. We have the momentum, and we have each other. Let's seize our chance to flip the Senate blue.
Thank you,
Jacky
* * *
##### `A personal note from Sen. Jacky Rosen:`
##### `My work in the Senate has always been defined by who I am and where I come from. Growing up as the granddaughter of immigrants and the daughter of a World War II veteran, my family instilled in me the values of hard work, determination, and persistence at a young age.`
##### `Now, I'm proud to fight tirelessly in the Senate to deliver progress for hardworking families like mine in Nevada and across our country. But with Donald Trump in the White House and Republicans in control of both houses of Congress, I need your grassroots support to keep up the fights that matter most.`
##### `Senate Democrats like me are the only thing standing in the way of Trump's extreme agenda that will hurt everyday Americans. That's why I need people like you on my side to help defend our progress and reclaim power from the GOP.`
##### `If you're with me, will you chip in now to help Democrats take back the Senate majority?`

Peter, for the
next ten days, this campaign has one goal:

Connect with as many undecided voters as possible before they fill out
their ballot.

That’s it. Do that, and we win. Simple, right? You’d think so, but there’s
a catch.

The catch is that MAGA Republicans are spending $100 million — over $1
million a day — to flood everyone’s phones, mailboxes, and TV screens with
pro-Rogers messages.

They're outspending us on the air 5 to 1. In a Senate race where the last
margin of victory was just 20,217 votes, letting MAGA Republicans get the
last word in could be what costs us this seat.

Luckily, we have a solid plan to prevent that from happening. Here's what
hitting our goal looks like:

* We stay on the air every single day. That way Michiganders hear from
us before they head to the polls.
* We expand our get-out-the-vote efforts. Knocking on a few more doors
and making a few extra calls could be the tipping point that hands us
the victory.
* We answer MAGA Republicans’ attacks before they stick. We don't let
them tell Michigan who I am.

Ten days is enough time to cover these bases, but only if we have the
resources to get it all done.

That’s why I’m counting on you, Peter,
and other members of this grassroots team
to have our back.

name: Gina
subject: I know it’s late, but
body:
Hi Peter, it’s Gina. I know it’s a
little late, but I wanted to send one last note before the day ends.

First, I just want to say thank you. I genuinely mean that from the bottom
of my heart. Since we launched this campaign a year ago, every single mile
traveled, every door knocked, and every conversation has been powered by
people like you. I’m grateful every day for what we have built together in
the last year.

I know how crowded your inbox gets, especially this close to Election Day.
Plenty of politicians send frantic emails while they have plenty of funds
to support their campaign.

But not our campaign. Many campaigns across this country aren’t going
against opponents like Greg Abbott, a 12-year incumbent with the financial
backing of multiple billionaires and even a trillionaire. We don’t have
that sort of support either, and to be honest, I don’t need it or want it.
This campaign was built from the ground up by everyday people, and that is
who I answer to. I’m running for Governor of Texas to fight for working
families, not the billionaires trying to buy our state.

Tonight, we’re facing the final official reporting deadline of this entire
campaign. Everything we do between now and November 3rd depends on what we
raise right now.

My team set an ambitious goal to raise $7 million before our final
official deadline closes tonight, and hitting it comes down to grassroots
supporters stepping up in this exact moment.

So I’m personally asking: will you make a donation today to power our

clean_body: I am not a career politician. I am stepping up to serve again because Montana is my home. | Peter, Early voting is already underway in Montana. Election Day is 10 days away. I want to make sure you know exactly who is asking for your support in these final days. My name is Kurt Alme. I am a Montana native. I was born in Great Falls. My dad taught high school math. I’ve spent my entire career serving and protecting Montana families. As Montana’s Budget Director and Revenue Director, I spearheaded two of the largest tax cuts in state history, balanced our state budget, and helped make Montana debt-free. I’ll fight to do it again in Washington. As Montana’s U.S. Attorney, nominated by President Trump and confirmed by the Senate twice, we went after violent criminals, expanded drug prevention and treatment, and targeted drug traffickers all the way to the cartels – and tore them out by their roots. [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1601-fr-nd&t=2&akid=13435%2E400544%2EG-rBtq)
After more than 20 years of running, I know that reaching the finish line takes preparation, persistence, and showing up when it counts. And as I held my ballot, I thought about the generations of Pueblo women who came before me and fought for the opportunities we have today. **Now, it’s our turn to show up, make our voices heard, and help shape the future of New Mexico. Every step counts, and every vote matters.**
Friend, this race is about building a future where _all_ New Mexicans can thrive. It’s about standing up to the attacks coming from the president and protecting the people and values that make our state special. It’s about investing in our schools, strengthening our healthcare system, and making life more affordable for hardworking families across New Mexico. **It’s about fighting for the future every New Mexican deserves.**

A federal judge threw out the Justice Department’s case against Virginia’s in-state tuition law. | | | Peter, When the news is heavy, it’s important to recognize and celebrate every bit of hard-won progress. **Undocumented students in Virginia can keep qualifying for in-state tuition! This is great news for many who have been working hard to pursue their education.** [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeabdGGvthn4g7RETlfNxxCD_F99e1on29UFO2iG0BJy0C9CM7JKnbjW2NFwecW1mdPl25Kwb5XD4RrJllCSBk0twLsEhvSeqQ1d4IOHB9Zj1yWqP9Fq7kypXFy0puRuVRiy4UcUfPPmPMw3b1ac5f2oFKs2XhF9pZI9A3pIOEUQI5mjTNCgGiMA2hwR6IwxG27cWsyxY5PXVMIHHG4rgR5LUpgLKyXLtvanGKbG3lYB72jTu9dH-7odC1KtQ_62_PoJjS-43-yyoVtJyaJnzxuF9XQ3XAXLIcaCdmdzygoe69xZRlvYj--IZ9MRgsj7bJ7kDn2zlMHKyH9GlnfNqQeiWq9pgmDWM1R3bpqQ7sp1Nu4biw9MXmfc8EP-asT82w/4v5/7QqKRUTNSjaER64bhDjhEA/h0/h001.xMcQkF1gTOPBWbSkxxRnwRFniUtvP8RtVZBLG1vFAkQ) Earlier this month, a federal judge dismissed the Justice Department’s lawsuit challenging Virginia’s in-state tuition law.1 _That means roughly 9,800 undocumented college students in Virginia can keep paying the same rates as their classmates._ 1 Immigrant youth have organized for years to win these laws, making higher education more affordable for working-class students who were being priced out because of their immigration status. **[Our Powered by Students campaign aims to train more students to organize their campuses and lead campaigns that win real change for all of us. Since June 2025, the Department of Justice has sued _every single state_ offering in-state tuition to undocumented immigrants. Virginia defended its law and became only the second state to win in court.1
Across the country, more than 525,000 undocumented students are enrolled in college. Roughly 180,000 of them are in states that have already stopped offering them in-state tuition, and another 210,000 attend school in states being sued right now.1

clean_body: A federal judge threw out the Justice Department’s case against Virginia’s in-state tuition law. | | | Peter, When the news is heavy, it’s important to recognize and celebrate every bit of hard-won progress. Undocumented students in Virginia can keep qualifying for in-state tuition! This is great news for many who have been working hard to pursue their education. Earlier this month, a federal judge dismissed the Justice Department’s lawsuit challenging Virginia’s in-state tuition law.1 That means roughly 9,800 undocumented college students in Virginia can keep paying the same rates as their classmates. 1 Immigrant youth have organized for years to win these laws, making higher education more affordable for working-class students who were being priced out because of their immigration status. | | Since June 2025, the Department of Justice has sued every single state offering in-state tuition to undocumented immigrants. Virginia defended its law and became only the second state to win in court.1 Across the country, more than 525,000 undocumented students are enrolled in college. Roughly 180,000 of them are in states that have already stopped offering them in-state tuition, and another 210,000 attend school in states being sued right now.1 If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | | | All students, no matter their immigration status or income level, should have the opportunity to access higher education, secure stable careers, and have financial stability and independence. Together, we’ll make sure they can. Thank you for being a part of this movement. — United We Dream * 1. “Judge Backs Virginia in Tuition Equity Case.” Inside Higher Ed. October 7, 2026. For too long, too many families in New Mexico have felt that Washington is scamming them. They see it in their daily lives. They see it at the grocery store, at the gas pump, and when the rent is due. While working people are stretched thin, too many people in power seem focused only on enriching themselves. We’re often told by those Washington politicians that division and gridlock are just the way things have to be. That real change is too hard, or that ordinary voices don't carry the same weight as money and influence. But I don't believe that has to be our future. I believe we can build a better one. We can choose a politics that focuses on practical solutions and common ground. One that remembers that at its heart, government should be about people. **That's what this campaign represents.** This campaign is not fueled by big checks from special interests, but by the support of everyday people across NM-02. It’s powered by teachers, nurses, small business owners, and working families giving what they can — $10, $25, or $50 at a time — because they believe in a better way forward.
